_comment: Data file for tools/regress.py. PASS iff every 'expect' substring appears in stdout+stderr (exit codes are NOT trusted - most ct.exe self-checks exit 0 even on mismatch). 'pin' regexes let 'regress.py --pin NAME' re-derive 'expect' from the matching full output lines after an INTENTIONAL, oracle-validated change. 'inputs' are repo-root-relative files that must exist or the check SKIPs. See docs/TESTING.md.

checks.name: tables-datafree-headers-current
expect: pack_tables: src/tables/ current
checks.notes: src/tables/ (the headers the engine includes the generated tables through, their data-free declarations, the storage and its layout asserts) is what tools/gen/pack_tables.py makes from today's shapes. A stale src/tables/ means a data-free Belthasar would declare a table the shapes no longer have, or refuse every pack (docs/ROM.md, 'The data-free Belthasar').

checks.notes: FF/FAA3 (CtMenuSaveLoad) run over saves/ct_real_save.srm -- a game CHRONO TRIGGER ITSELF saved -- so every field printed comes out of that cartridge file through the ROM's own 8-record table (disasm/notes/boot_loader.md S6). A wrong record address, bank or length moves one of them: loc/tile/bits are record 3 ($00:0100+0x10), party is record 0 (+0x0580 -> $7E:2980), gold is record 1 ($2C53), storyline is record 4's first byte ($7F:0000). 'era' and 'chapter' additionally grade the two ROM string lookups the load screen shows -- the per-location nibble table $FF:D296 -> $FF:D396 (C2/D3AD) and the storyline threshold walk $FF:D024 -> $FF:D03E (C2/D266) -- against the strings the ORACLE draws for this same save. Slots 1/2 EMPTY grades the FF/F9C4 gate's signature arm. The chapter string carries its LEADING SPACES because the ROM does not centre it -- the pen starts at the block's left edge and those spaces are what position it (measured on the oracle's own rendered tiles), so the table holds the string verbatim. | 2026-10-10 re-pinned on the recipe-made fixture (name_saved): gold 1105 -> 1035, every other field unchanged. The recipe's game carries 1035 G: the oracle's own $2C53 when it saved (build/recipes/name_saved.state) and the battery's record 1; the cartridge's Load screen with this battery equals the port's pixel for pixel (python tools/boot_loader_cmp.py saves/ct_real_save.srm: 57344 / 57344), era and chapter strings included.

mutations.replace: if (menuLoaderOn && ((menuPhase == 1 && menuT == 15 && 0) || (menuPhase == 4 && menuBri <= 0))) {   /* MUT */
mutations.why: C2/8000's MODE-0 SHORT CIRCUIT (28042 LDA $7F0061 / BNE) is what makes a blank cart skip the load screen entirely and reboot into a new game. Without it the boot stops on an empty slot list.

mutations.replace: (void)0;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: the title frame's fnv32 here is the ORACLE's own hash of the same 256x224 RGB, and the colours in it arrive through the vblank hook $7E:388B, which DMAs the palette shadow $7E:2200 into CGRAM every frame. Without that upload frame 0 composes out of an all-zero palette and the hash has to move.

mutations.replace: if (0) t->exitFlag = 1;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: the title sequence's only exit is $7E:5BB7 `STA $7F0060`, and it is the overlay's own task $5B99 that decides it -- not the host. Without the flag, scene 433's 0x000F test never leaves the attract and the boot never reaches location 0, so every line after the fade disappears.

checks.notes:
THE COLD BOOT OF A BLANK CARTRIDGE, end to end (disasm/notes/boot_loader.md). Every line is a different ROM decision: C0/0057's SRAM scan finding nothing ($7F0061=0), scene 0's 0x001B glb[0x60]==0 arm changing to the title location 433, the attract stage-0 `FF 02` leaving the field engine for the $C3 sequence engine (whose first frame is now the mode-7 PENDULUM, not the settled logo -- title_intro.md), START leaving $7F0060=1 behind ($7E:5BB7) -- pressed at frame 90, because $7E:5B99 is not installed until the sequence's 50th frame and the ROM IGNORES the button before that (measured on the oracle: a press at boot 150 leaves $7F0060 and $0070 at zero for the next 120 frames). This check used to press at frame 40 and pass, because the port used to do START host-side instead of running the overlay's own task. The fade line is the rest of that correction: $5B99 installs $7E:34AB, which becomes $34C2 and walks $038D 15 -> 0 before $7E:0000 goes up, so the reboot is sixteen frames after the button, not the same frame so the reboot lands back on 433 and its 0x000F test now exits to location 0, and -- crucially -- C2/8000's MODE-0 SHORT CIRCUIT: with $7F0061 still 0 the load screen NEVER DRAWS, it wipes and reboots into the new game. The ATB line is the proof it reached the new-game arm. 'sequence: 2 drawn ... fnv32=34C88B76' is the composed title frame's hash, and it EQUALS the hash of the ORACLE's own framebuffer at the same settled frame (256x224 RGB, cold boot f1600) -- so it grades the bake and the compositing against the cartridge, not against itself. Measured against the oracle: f94 $0A00=0 -> f95 $7F0061=1 -> f131 $0A00=3.

RE-TIMED (+43) when the title's SETUP HOLD landed. $7E:5978 keeps working for 43 frames after it loads the song, with the NMI still disabled and the screen black, so the port now holds too -- which pushed every machine frame 43 later in the boot. The START press has to stay on the far side of MACHINE frame 48, which is where $7E:5B99 enters the task list (measured: `--monitor 7E0920:12 --from build/_ti/f140.state --diff` shows it appear at f48); at frame 90 it would now land at machine frame ~22 and the ROM would ignore it, which is the SECOND time this exact trap has bitten these checks. The cursor-press SPACING is unchanged. || RE-PINNED 2026-10-01 AT THE RULE FLIP (CLAUDE.md: the infinitely fast CPU, the line cuts and NMI-on work free are the default now; tools/rule_flip/attract.json): PASS as is -- passes unchanged under the switches (the triage's CONTENT flag came from pin lines that are a subset of the expect lines; every expect line is printed under the rule on the final binary). The boot's SRAM scan, the title's swing frame 0 and the blank-cart loader come before any song load the rule prices.

mutations.find: int line = y + 1;                                // ⚠ the SNES renders scanlines 1..224
mutations.replace: int line = y;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: The SNES renders scanlines 1..224 and it is `line`, not `line-1`, that enters the mode-7 matrix and selects the sprite row (snes/ppu.c ppu_runLine). Off by one the whole texture shears by one row of the affine transform -- invisible in a thumbnail, thousands of pixels against the oracle.

mutations.find: int cout = (word >> 15) & 1;                       // ⭐ bit 7 of the old $F8
mutations.replace: int cout = 0;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: $7E:31BF clears $F6 (and so $F7) and then ROLs the WORD at $F7, which rotates BIT 7 OF THE STALE $F8 into its middle ADC. Dropping that carry is exactly the reason this note used to call the matrix underivable and bake a captured stream; with it the whole swing computes. The mutation puts the matrix one unit off wherever the carry was set.

mutations.replace: b = (uint8_t)(b >> 1);  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C3/0D5E's `SEC / ROR A` is what makes every sprite it emits 16x16 -- the drawer builds the high-OAM byte from the TOP down, two bits per sprite. Without the set bit the fourteen copyright sprites become 8x8 and the block loses three quarters of itself.

checks.notes: THE TITLE INTRO'S FIRST 745 FRAMES -- the mode-7 pendulum, the copyright block and the clock's spiral-in -- against the ORACLE'S OWN FRAMEBUFFER, not a hash of our own output (memory: check-vs-own-reference). tools/title_intro_cmp.py runs the engine to a swing frame, runs the oracle to the boot frame that swing frame IS (k + 141), and compares all 57344 pixels. 0 and 100 sit in the COPYRIGHT window (fourteen subscreen sprites CGADSUB adds to BG1), 400/500/588 in the mode-7-only stretch, 620 has the clock spiralling out of the bob and 745 is the first MODE-2 frame. Two frames are in the list for a specific reason and must not be dropped: 150 is where the swing moves FASTEST and is the only one that notices a one-frame slip in the matrix; 10 and 400 are where the $F8 carry inside $7E:31BF actually moves pixels (9939 and 1151 of them) -- at 0/100/300/500/588 the same mutation survives, which is how the first version of this check failed to grade it. The logo phase past 745 is title-intro-logo-vs-oracle. THREE things are deliberately NOT pinned with mutations, each confirmed by a SURVIVING one: the sine routine's CPX #$0200 carry (always 0 -- the spiral's angle never reaches $100), the PPU's per-line sprite limits (20 is the most any scanline of the sequence carries) and the largeField clip: removing it changes nothing at any frame of the swing (measured 110/130/200/400/580), and a mutation nothing can kill is not a grade.

mutations.find: int valid = layer == 0 ? 0x2000 : 0x4000;          // bit 13 = "for BG1", bit 14 = "for BG2"
mutations.replace: int valid = layer == 0 ? 0x4000 : 0x2000;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: The TRIGGER logo ripples because BG3's tilemap is read as OFFSET-PER-TILE in mode 2, and bit 13 is what says an entry belongs to BG1. Swapping the two bits silences the ripple on BG1 and applies it to the (static) pendulum on BG2 -- the exact mistake of reading the table as a scroll.

mutations.replace: if (0) v = t->tgt[i];  /* MUT */
mutations.why: $7E:5D71 clamps each CHRONO letter at its OWN target ($0050,X) -- five different targets, five different speeds. Without the clamp the letters keep sliding right forever instead of settling into the word.

mutations.replace: if (n < 0) { r[0] = 0; continue; }  /* MUT */
mutations.why: A palette job that walks past its target does not stop at the last blended value: FD/E8AC copies $7E:2000 (the base palette) straight back over the shadow. Without that copy the clock hands keep the blend's zeroed BLUE for the rest of the sequence, so the settled title is the wrong colour.

mutations.replace: t->l.bri = 0x0F;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: $7E:34C2's fade is the brightness shadow $038D, and C3/08D0 pushes it to $2100 between the vblank hooks and the tasks -- so it belongs to the LATCH, one frame behind the cells, exactly like the scrolls. Pinning it at full brightness leaves the last frames of the sequence undimmed.

checks.notes: THE TITLE INTRO'S LOGO PHASE -- BG MODE 2 with offset-per-tile -- against the ORACLE'S OWN FRAMEBUFFER, all 57344 pixels per frame. 800 is mid letter-slide, 1040 has the TRIGGER logo scrolled in and the clock hands in their yellow flash (the kind-4 palette job), 1290 is inside the ripple's damping window, 1500 is after both palette jobs have restored the base palette, 1989 is the settled title on the last frame before the script hands over, and 1994/2000/2007 are inside $7E:34C2's fade-out ($038D 15 -> 0). 2007 is the LAST frame the sequence owns: at 2008 the ROM's main loop sees $7E:0000 and writes INIDISP = $80 about 37 scanlines into the display, so the oracle's frame is the top of a dim title over black -- a mid-frame blank this engine has no scanline model for, and a frame the port has already rebooted past. This is the frame the port used to BAKE (src/data/title_screen.h, deleted): it is now computed. The PPU's 32-sprite / 34-sliver per-line limits are transliterated but deliberately NOT pinned: the densest scanline of the whole sequence carries 20 sprites (counted from the oracle's OAM at boot 1230), so raising the cap changes nothing and the mutation SURVIVED -- see title_intro.md section 7.2. Full tier because the late frames need ~2400 engine frames each (53s for the set); the first 745 frames are the quick check title-intro-swing-vs-oracle.

checks.name: title-intro-machine-vs-oracle-wram
expect: ti-sim scripted: boot 141..2148, 62278 values checked, 0 mismatches
ti-sim button:   boot 141..757, 19157 values checked, 0 mismatches
ti-sim shoulder: boot 141..757, 19157 values checked, 0 mismatches

checks.notes: THE TITLE SEQUENCE'S MACHINE against the ORACLE'S LIVE WRAM, cell by cell: the script's sixteen registers, the mode-7 matrix, the clock's spiral, the letter slide, the ripple, the frame counter, the palette shadow, the task list, the brightness trio $038D/$038E/$038F, $0070 and $7F0060. Three scenarios, and each window ends where the SEQUENCE does -- the frame $7E:34C2 sets $7E:0000 -- which the harness derives from its own done flag rather than hard-coding: 'scripted' is the script's own handover at boot 2132, 'button' is a press at boot 741, 'shoulder' is the same press with L held, which still fades but leaves $7F0060 at ZERO (the branch that drops the boot into the attract demo). ⚠ WHAT THIS GRADES IS THE DERIVATION, NOT THE SHIPPED C: tools/ti_sim.py is the python model the port was transcribed from. The C is graded on pixels by title-intro-swing/logo-vs-oracle and, for the START-to-reboot chain specifically, by boot-natural-blank-cart's fade line. C3/09A4's watcher is modelled and its shadows $0388/$0389/$038A are compared, but they never move in this sequence (the title latches both to its own song), so the watcher's BODY cannot be graded here -- the engine check title-sequence-sound-reaches-driver does it, by counting posts. A fourth thing cannot be graded here and is deliberately not pinned: the fade's step PERIOD $038E is 1 in this sequence, so hard-coding it is indistinguishable from reloading it (mutation written, SURVIVED, deleted). Both halves are needed: the pixel checks drive no buttons, so without this one the START, L/R and fade branches have no cell-level pin at all.

mutations.replace: if True:  # MUT
mutations.why: $7E:5B99's second look at the pad is `BIT #$30` -- L or R -- and it is what decides whether $7F0060 is left behind. Ignoring it makes every exit look like a START, and the 'shoulder' scenario is the only place in the whole suite where that shows.

mutations.replace: self.listdel(self.pend, 0x34AB); self.listadd(self.pend, 0x34C2)  # MUT
mutations.why: $7E:34AB leaves through $39B1, which writes the NEW task into the SLOT the old one was running in -- not through delete-then-install, which would drop it into the first free slot instead. The task-list compare is what sees the difference.

mutations.replace: self.mail[1] = 0x30  # MUT
mutations.why: $7E:34AB's `LDX #$0040 / STX $1E01` is what the driver reads out of $2141 for the music fade. The mailbox is compared against the oracle's own $7E:1E00..$1E03 every frame the sequence owns it, so a wrong parameter byte shows immediately -- and the frames before the exit read $30 there, which is what makes this mutation a real test rather than a coincidence.

checks.notes:
THE TITLE SEQUENCE'S MUSIC AND ITS EXIT SOUND, through the real mailbox and the real SPC. The setup starts the title's own song ($7E:5AA5 `LDA #$30 / JSR $375F` -- id into $1E01, $10 into $1E00, $FFFF over the other two, then `JSL $C7:0004`), and C7/0A39 overwrites $1E02/$1E03 with that song's own record ($C7:241D + id*2 = $06/$C0), which is why every later line reads `40 00 06`. Then $7E:34AB stages $1E00=$81 with `LDX #$0040 / STX $1E01` (a 16-bit store, so $1E01=$40 AND $1E02=$00) and fifteen frames later $7E:34D5 stages $1E00=$F0 ALONE. Both are >= $80, so C7/061C writes all four bytes straight to $2140-$2143. `posted -> $1E00=00` is the anti-vacuity half: the emulated Akao driver actually READ the command (C7/0192 clears the byte on the way out), so this cannot rot green by staging into a mailbox nobody services. ⭐ ALL FOUR BYTES ARE PINNED, $1E03 included. An earlier version of this check deliberately left it unpinned, on the belief that C7/01A1's record write-back was not ported and the $05 there was the port's own history -- BOTH halves of that were wrong: the write-back has been in src/audio.c all along ($C7:0A39, the `SM8(m, 0x1E02, scalar)` pair), and the $05 was song 0's record because the port was not playing the title's song at all. The byte is the ROM's, so it is pinned. ⭐ The count line is the anti-repeat half: THREE posts and only three (the setup's song, $34AB's fade, $34D5's stop). A fourth would mean C3/09A4's watcher had fired, i.e. $375F's `STA $0389` was missing -- an extra `staged` line alone would not fail a substring check, so the count is what grades it. ⚠ The watcher's own BODY is still ungradeable here, and the mutation that dropped $375F's `STA $0389` SURVIVED and was deleted: the port SEEDS $0389 from the oracle's WRAM (the seed is taken after the setup has run), so the setup's write is redundant in this architecture and removing it changes nothing. C3/09A4 is written out because it is the NMI's other half and it is why $375F writes both shadows -- not because this sequence can fire it. The `$2143 wait 6 frame(s)` half is the setup's own spin ($7E:5AAA `LDA $2143 / AND #$0F / BEQ`), and the 6 is MEASURED by the port's own emulated driver, not baked: the oracle spins boot 133..139, just over six frames, and the port's SPC answers on the same schedule. ⚠ The port does not make the ENGINE lose those frames the way the ROM's blocked CPU does; the SPC time is debited (cycleCarry) so it is not advanced twice, but nothing about the title's start is pinned to the boot's frame number.

checks.notes: THE $A4 GROUP SCHEDULER'S CADENCE. battle_facing_engine.md carried this subsystem as NOT DERIVED, and two things were blocked on it: the idle dwell's stateless mean-10 replay, and the $5E0D/$974A split (battle_enemy_move_modes.md V19), whose commit rides on this counter. WHY IT WAS NEVER FOUND: the counter is FOUR INSTRUCTIONS IN BANK CF -- CF/E477 `INC $A4`, CF/E479 `LDA $A4 / CMP #04 / BNE`, CF/E47F `STZ $A4` -- and every previous hunt searched bank C1, where the battle logic is. Bank C1 only BORROWS the counter: C1/10A4 snapshots it into $993B, C1/10A9 dispatches the group (A = $A4 from C1/2DA2; C1/3234 is three copies of `DEC A / BNE / DEC $A4 / JMP <group>`, so the counter is both the credit and the group id), and C1/10B3 restores it. That restore is exactly why `--monitor \"00A4:1\" --diff --writer` never shows a decrement -- they are undone inside the same frame. One extra bump exists at C1/34A4, gated on $A4 != $993B and $A4 < 3. THE RATE, MEASURED ON FOUR CAPTURES: taking the CF:E481 wrap as the cycle boundary, the wrap intervals are the SAME repeating triple 7,7,6 in bat2, bat3, bat9 and forest_battle_3hetake -- 3 full 0..3 cycles per 20 frames -- differing only in phase. Counting the increments themselves in five-frame windows gives 3 every time: THE COUNTER ADVANCES THREE TIMES EVERY FIVE FRAMES, the same shape as this file's move cadence (mvCadAcc += 4) one step slower. The ported 3-of-5 accumulator reproduces the oracle's bat3 interval sequence EXACTLY (7,6,7,7,6,7,7,6), at a one-frame phase offset; phase is capture-dependent on the oracle side too (bat2 f3, bat9 f3, forest3 f4). ⚠ ANCHORED, NOT PRICED. The 3-of-5 is a measured rate, not a count of ROM work: CF/E470 is a DMA/upload service pass (`LDA $CCF96F,X / STA $2116`, `LDA #80 / STA $420B`), so how often it runs is a property of the upload queue -- the same species as the action pre-roll's U. Four captures agreeing on 7,7,6 is what justifies the constant, not a derivation of the queue's drain rate. ⚠ NOTHING CONSUMES $A4 YET. C1/0023 ends `JSL CD/000C / JSL CD/0012 / BNE ->1003C / JMP C1/34DB`: the entry-fade loop BLOCKS until the band's steps finish and the fall-through arms the ladder with window 0x30 (C1/34F7 `LDA #30 / STA $5DF1,Y`). Both arms (C1/34DB window 0x30, C1/35AE window 0x28) share one shape and gate per seat on $A09B,X: zero -> the window, non-zero -> window 0. TWO THINGS THE PLAN HAD WRONG, both measured before porting: (1) $5DF1 has exactly FOUR writers in the 4 MB image -- C1/34EB/34F7 (#00/#30) and C1/35BE/35CA (#00/#28) -- so window 0x20, which the plan lists beside 0x30, is armed NOWHERE and is not a gap; (2) C1/34DB looked unreachable (no JSR, JMP or JSL anywhere targets the C1/0042 address, because that address is CODE, the boot's tail, not a vector) -- but `--monitor \"7E5DF1:8\" --diff --writer` shows window 0x30 live in bat3, bat9 AND forest_wait_ambush_active, armed there at f360 by C1:34FF. The enemy AI runs one entry per turn on the ROM's own pointer ($B1D4/$B1E4, C1/8C3E + C1/8CF9): GATO's op 00 move is a TURN WITH NO ACTION (the cartridge's f892), so his song comes one ATB later (cartridge $A013 f1151 = fixture f925); the eval writes $AEE3 = the op it pre-reads (C1/8CE0 -- the cartridge's 01 00 01 at f376, 00 00 06 at f635); and the turn no longer draws a target (the cartridge's turn draws only the damage pipeline), so HP values and targets that ride the RNG index moved to the cartridge's draw count. The Hetakes' op 00 turns run instead of being 'aborted' by the mover (C1/8461 never reads $98A7). ==== 2026-09-18 (c), RE-PINNED (an enemy action closes at its script's op 01, disasm/notes/battle_boot_turns.md sec. 5): An enemy action now ends as every action does in the ROM -- C1/40CE's `$9876` test after the script's op 01 (C1/4CF7 -> C1/4D00) plus C1/40D3-41BA's tail -- instead of on a stored span (CT_SPAN_ENEMY_AVG 202 for every non-GATO enemy, GATO's 157 / 224 / 311). Measured on the cartridge: every enemy action closes `$9876 = 1` + 5 frames with a PC victim; the forest Hetake's six spans are now the cartridge's (177 202 188 189 192 187, were 202 each). GATO's attack A is 153 (cartridge 157), attack B 213 (222 / 226), the song 300 (311): the difference is the cartridge's LAG frames -- the action loop's every-8th-frame job (C1/10FA -> C1/0C2D, C1/1C3A's 384-byte copy) overrunning the NMI through his flurry, the C0/C4 pre-roll's decompressions -- a CPU overrun the port has no clock for (named, not fitted). The close then exposed the EFFECT TEARDOWN the main loop runs (C1/10A0 JSL CD/0009 -> CD/04AA -> CD/0453, ported): after an action whose programs ran (`$CCEA` set), 21 frames with no main-loop iteration, `$CCEA` / `$CCA2` cleared, the colours and layer shadows put back -- the port had never cleared `$CCEA` (a second program held its action forever) and lost none of those frames. Song end -> GATO's next attack is 281 frames against the cartridge's 279 (was 257). So the fight after each GATO action runs 4 / 11 frames earlier, and where that changes which ATB fills first, the order of later actions and the RNG draws that ride on it. PHOTO MOVED f1041 -> f1016: the same moment, found by the action's identity with the OLD binary reproducing the pinned hash through the anchor (run-off-open#1+170); the SAME picture (hash unchanged). ==== 2026-09-18, THE MAIN LOOP'S TWO-FRAME ITERATION (the zelda3 model; disasm/notes/oracle_logical_frames.md §4). The battle's idle loop waits twice per iteration (C1/109D, C1/10BD): frame A runs the walk dispatch and C1/10BB STZ $E5, frame B C1/10C4 INC $E5 and the tail (timers, cursors, handlers), then the next head's C1/8121 INC $0027. The three rates this file carried -- the logic tick at 2.5 frames, the $A4 INC at 3 of 5, the mode pass at 4 of 5 -- were fits of the REAL cartridge's lagging iterations; the logical oracle runs every iteration in two frames, and the port now does: $A4 is the NMI's CF/E3F8 INC on $A013 = 0 and $E5 != 0, an enemy turn is C1/4058's two waits (CT_BATTLE_ENEMY_THINK 3 -> 2, the demo's C1/4058 3 -> 2), the first head is the entrance loop's end + CT_BATTLE_BOOT_CPU 0. battle-gato-fight-vs-logical-oracle grades the whole GATO fight against the logical oracle frame for frame; the ATB fills ~20% faster than on the lagging cartridge (song end -> attack A 231 against 279). C1/8443-8448, the end epilogue: `LDA $26 / STA $29AD`, right before the C1/B442 block->sheet writeback, hands the ADVANCED cursor back. ROM-wide the accessors are exactly C1/800A (read), C1/8445 (write), and the MENU's C2/805E + C2/E6A8 (`LDA $0D00 / STA $29AD`, its own cursor on exit); bank C0 never touches it, so between fights it simply persists in WRAM.
HOW THE WRONG LAW GOT PINNED: battle_facing_engine.md SESSION-9 recorded 'the battle boot ZEROES $26 (oracle f234: A0->00)'. expect: atbload min=36 base=35 B158=48 36 66 AFAB=13 01 31

checks.notes:
THE INITIAL ATB LOAD IS THE ROM'S NORMALISER FD/B8F8-B93A, not a fitted constant. `load[i] = $B158[i] - (MIN - 1)`, MIN = smallest $B158 over present, nonzero combatants. $B158 is the reload (FD/B7EF..B85B: `0x69 - 6*speed(block+0x38, clamp 16) + CC2E31[(speed-1)+(bs&7)*16]`), and the normaliser's scan (FD/B8FD: initial min = slot 0 unconditionally, then X=1..0x0A keeps a candidate iff $B158,X < min AND != 0 AND $AEFF,X != FF) then subtracts min-1 from every present nonzero slot in place (FD/B923-B933).

Ours prints exactly `min=36 base=35 B158=48 36 66 AFAB=13 01 31`. None of the three matches `-0x47` (which would give 01/EF-clamped-00/1F).

==== RE-PIN 2026-08-29 (disasm/notes/battle_ui_sfx_sites.md). USER REPORT (translated from Portuguese): 'the battle hud's sound does not play'. Both posts used to live ONLY in battleMenuFrozen(), whose one call site is `if (wasFrozen)` -- so with no action animating (the normal case) the whole battle HUD was SILENT. Two structural corrections, both ROM-derived:
(1) THE CHIME IS THE ENQUEUE'S, NOT THE WINDOW'S. C1/1B41 has no entry of its own (whole-image scans for `20 41 1B` / `4C 41 1B` / `22 41 1B C1` find no bank-C1 caller): it is the FALL-THROUGH tail of the ready-enqueue routine C1/1B19, reached only via the dispatcher C1/0003 table entry [1] from the single site C1/856D, on the rising edge of $93EE+7*pc. So it is posted at battleEnqueue, and the expect line is now `ready-chime seat<k>`. Two things the old window-rising-edge model could not produce, both oracle-measured: the ROM chimes AGAIN for a second PC while the first PC's window is open (f402, $95D5=00, $A013=00), and a submenu / target-select cancelled BACK to the command window posts the BLIP, never the chime.
(2) THE BLIP IS THE DISPATCHER'S, ON THE BUTTON EDGE, BEFORE THE HANDLER. All 29 sites are `JSR C1/1B55` followed by `JMP <handler>` inside C1/115F's dispatch, so a no-op nav still blips (oracle f129/f173/f153/f197: blip with no monitored byte changing). Ours tested `$95DC != oldCur`, which is the wrong SHAPE and covered 1 of 7 contexts. battleUiBlipDispatch now reproduces C1/115F's order (target-select -> tech -> item -> command level) and is called from BOTH menu passes, so the tech/item submenus and target-select blip too. checks.notes:
THE DEAD FLAG IS CLEARED AT BATTLE END and this port never cleared it. C1/EAE8 is `TDC / STA $5E4A,X` -- block+0x1D := 0, the WHOLE byte -- looped over the 3 seats via C1/E9A3's block base, and BOTH end tails call it immediately before the writeback: C1/83F9 `JSR C1/EAE8 / JSR C1/B442` (victory) and C1/843D the same (defeat). So the cleared byte rides the block->sheet copy out to $2600.
WHY NO CAPTURE COULD SEE IT: a PC only carries block+0x1D bit7 into the END of a fight if it entered flagged dead or died during it, and no shipped seed does either -- so the clear was unreachable and its absence invisible. gato_deadmarle sets Marle's char-sheet status byte $266D bit7 before the fight.
ORACLE: the same patch on the LakeSnes state (gato_wait, $266D |= 0x80) -- $266D reads 80 for the whole fight and then `f2257 7E266D=00*(C1:B475)`, i.e. the writeback carries EAE8's zero out. Ours prints `battle-deadclear seat1 +0x1D 80 -> 00`, and the unpatched gato_t0 prints the line zero times (the trace only fires when a flag was actually set), so this check cannot pass by accident on a clean seed.
ORDERING, and it is the ROM's: the reward grant SKIPS dead PCs (block+0x1D bit7) and the ROM's rewards (C1/F93E) run BEFORE the EAE8 clear -- so a PC dead at the end gets no rewards AND still leaves with the flag clear; the field re-derives "down" from curHP == 0. WHAT THIS DOES NOT PORT: the ROM's per-refresh death SWEEP C1/B279 (writer C1:B28B), which re-derives the flag from curHP on every sweep; our engine only SETS it at damage-apply. That half is still open.

checks.notes:
EVERY PC TECH WAS COMPLETELY SILENT, and the cause was not a missing opcode -- it was the TABLE. PC scripts do not live in the bank-CD tables the enemy arm reads: they resolve through CD/5EC6[$9877*2] (physicals) and CD/5EF0[$9877*2] (techs) into BANK CE. Both read sites are explicit in the ROM (C1/442C and C1/4617), and C1/4623 `LDA $CE0000,X` right after the tech one names the bank. Arming the interpreter with the enemy tables produced `anim(ptr=CD/0000 parsed=0)` -- no script at all -- so the op-0x78 sound opcodes the tech scripts carry (Cyclone `78 FF`, Slash `78 53` + `78 4F`, ...) were never reached. Op 0x78 itself was already ported: C1/619E is `$1E01 = operand / $1E00 = ($9895-0x78)+0x18 / $1E02 = #80`.
IT ALSO NEEDED 16 OPCODE LENGTHS. A track STOPS on an unresolved opcode, and the PC scripts use ops the shipped length law could not resolve -- the canonical `A9 nn 4C BB 75` scan misses any handler with an instruction between the LDA and the JMP (0x2D: `LDA #01 / STA $CFFF / JMP`) or whose tail is reached by a branch. Each length here is the ROM's own advance (the value live in A at that handler's `JMP C1/75BB`), cross-checked against the handler's `INY / LDA [$E6],Y` operand-fetch count -- length == operands + 1 in every case. Two traps worth recording: ops 0x6C and 0xC0 both do `LDA #imm / STA $8E` or `$8F` MODE stores that look like an advance (C0's real advance is 5 via C1/6F2C `LDA $8E`, and its site CE/37D0 `C0 2B 18 80 07 71` only decodes sanely at 5); and several ops have a SECOND tail advancing 0, which is not a length but the PARK arm (re-run me next frame), exactly like op 0x24's wait. Op 0x80 is genuinely VARIABLE-LENGTH -- C1/621B masks its first operand with #0F as a byte COUNT and advances n+1 -- so it goes through battleAnimOpLenAt, not the fixed table.
ORACLE, a real Cyclone cast (gato_wait with Crono's learned-tech bit $2837 := 0x80, driven through the tech menu): `f538 7E9877=01*(C1:45C2)` dispatches selector 01, then `f587 7E1E01=91*(C1:61A4)` and `f737 7E1E01=FF*(C1:61A4)`, both pan 80 -- C1:61A4 is the op-0x78 handler's own `STA $1E01`. Ours posts id 91 then id FF, same order, same ids. STRONGER: the oracle's pose-publish stream for the caster (`--monitor 7E967B:1 --writer`, writer C1:4307) reads 47, D5, 7F, 80, B7, 81 and ours publishes exactly 47, D5, 7F, 80, B7, 81 -- the whole caster animation, byte for byte, not just the sounds.
SCOPE, stated rather than assumed: PC PHYSICALS stay on their existing pinned route. Their sound already works (op 0x7C at a measured rel) and their motion/pose bake is what every PC pin grades. Only techs -- which had no sound path at all -- are armed.
ONE BOUNDARY WAS NEEDED AND IS MARKED AS SUCH: battleAscSetPos now declines to move a PC caster. The tech's track 0 issues its own slides for the caster while our validated tech ROUTE already drives him, and two drivers showed immediately -- the route's snap moved f450 -> f455 with identical geometry. That is a PORT boundary, not a ROM claim (the ROM has one driver), and it is the same split the pose engine already used for PCs. Two further pose gates were tried and REMOVED after measuring that they changed no pixel at all.
SIDE EFFECT, oracle-confirmed and re-pinned rather than suppressed: the tech's script also arms the VICTIM's window, so enemies now FLINCH during a PC tech. field-battle-tech-cyclone-whirl-asma moved for exactly that -- the pixel diff is a 55x55 block centred on GATO -- and the oracle publishes GATO's hurt assembly 0x0C at f748 of the same cast (`7E967B=0C*(C1:4307)`), so the flinch is real ROM behaviour this port was missing.

The ids and their ORDER are what is graded.

Op 0xC0 in particular is only reached by techs beyond this fixture's cast (e.g. sel 3D), so a mutation of ITS length SURVIVES this check -- measured, not assumed. Its value is still ROM-derived and double-checked by decoding a real site (CE/37D0 `C0 2B 18 80 07 71`, which only decodes sanely at 5). checks.notes:
The user report 'on the second hit of crono's critical attack there was no SFX'. Crono's crit dispatches its OWN anim script -- $9877 = 0x01 -> CD/5EC6[01] = CE/03CC -- whose w1.t0 carries TWO sound opcodes where the normal attack CE/0380 carries one: `1E 2B | 36 | 7C | 72 0D | 03 31 | 36 | 35 | 7D | 03 32 | ...`. The second is op 0x7D (C1/61F5), and it reads the OTHER table -- CD/6DAC[$A4E7], not CD/6D4C -- so for weapon 01 the two slashes are DIFFERENT sounds, 4F then 40. Oracle ground truth, crit forced by patching $5E72/$5EF2 := FF on an IN-BATTLE state (a pre-battle patch is overwritten -- C1/CF3B recomputes block+0x45 at boot): crit #1 dispatch f239 -> f271 id 4F pan 84 -> f312 id 40 pan 84; crit #2 dispatch f824 -> f859 id 4F pan A5 -> f900 id 40 pan A5. WHAT THIS GRADES, in three independent ways: the two IDs come from two different ROM tables (a port that reused CD/6D4C would print id=4F twice); the rel GAP is 71-30 = 41, the oracle's own on both crits, and it is anchored on the first POST not on the dispatch because the leap distance moves the first post (32 vs 35) and not the gap; and both posts carry the SAME pan, as the oracle's do -- Crono does not move between slashes. Mutation-tested: deleting the 0x7D branch drops the second line, and perturbing CT_PC_SFX_CRIT_2ND moves rel off 71. RE-DERIVED (the crit approach is the ROM's own slide, not a box-stopped hop). The crit script's `1E 2B` super is CE/D795 = `0C | 02 26 | D0 | 98 02 28 | D1 | 1F`: speed 4, windup loop, hide shadow, SLIDE to resolver mode 0x28, show shadow, pop. checks.notes: Lockstep C-port frame: CtPortRunFrame (C-maintained OBJ priority + CtBuildFieldOAMFull into g_ram) vs the oracle OAM region.  ==== 2026-08-08: CtBuildFieldOAMFull RETIRED, and the swap was chosen so this check did not go vacuous. CtPortRunFrame used to end in CtBuildFieldOAMFull -- a copy-stub that stood in for the whole record pipeline by deriving the screen position from the world position (CtActorScreenCoords) and decoding the tiles out of the ROM (CtDecodeSpriteAssembly). Both halves of the real pipeline are graded now (C0/B788's emit by --sweepdrain, C0/B309's stage-2 copy by --sweepstage2), so the stub is gone. ⚠ THE OBVIOUS SWAP WOULD HAVE BEEN A MEMCPY GRADE: CtPortCopyWramFromOracle pulls the oracle's ENTIRE WRAM into g_ram, records included, so a bare CtBuildFieldOAM would read the oracle's $7F:4BC0 and write back the oracle's own OAM. Running CtAnimDrawPass FIRST is what keeps it honest -- C0/B701's reposition arm recomputes each piece's placed X (xd + $0A00) and its CLAMPED Y into the record's +0/+1, so those two bytes per piece are C-produced before stage 2 copies them out. MEASURED, four mutations: breaking ctOamEmit's X placement -> 2424 mismatches over 180 frames (so the emit IS graded end-to-end here, which it never was before); mis-addressing stage 2's Y read -> 2424; replacing ctOamEmit's Y CLAMP with the plain add the old builder used -> STILL GREEN, i.e. the clamp never binds on this scenario (that is exactly why the old defect was invisible for so long, and it is a characterised blind spot, not coverage); and deleting the CtAnimDrawPass call -> also still green, because a correct emit only rewrites the stubbed records with the same values, so the producer's ABSENCE cannot be seen in the OAM bytes. THAT LAST ONE IS WHY THE LINE NOW CARRIES `C0/B701 emit ran on 606 objects`: it is the denominator that makes the producer's presence assertable when its effect is not -- remove the call and it reads 0. ⚠ Still 4-PIECE: CtPortRunFrame's cTplAttr cache re-injects tiles 0..3 only, so pieces 4..11 of a class-1/2 sprite would keep the oracle's priority byte. Inert here (every object on this scenario is class 0) and stated rather than silently widened, because nothing in this check could grade the wider case.  ==== 2026-08-08b: the priority injection is no longer 4-PIECE, and the fix was to stop RE-DERIVING rather than to widen the derivation. The obvious repair was to teach CtDecodeSpriteAssembly the class-1/2 geometry -- the per-class frame-record stride ($28/$50/$78, applied by the ROM through the hardware multiplier at C0/CBDC with $4202 = the frame and $4203 = the stride), the offsets at stride-pieces*2 ($20/$40/$60), and the two class-2 tile-numbering variants whose extra $10 jumps at a different piece in each. All of that is already derived AND PORTED AND GRADED as C0/CAD9's frame half (--sweepcad9, 165888/165888, all four classes and both class-2 geometries), so re-deriving it here would have been a second model of one computation -- the exact defect just removed from CtBuildFieldOAM. Instead the per-tile Y offset now comes from where that producer staged it: $7F:4800 + $1700,X + e*8, +4 (ctOamEmit reads it as CT_STAGE(o+2) off its $4802 base, and --checkdecode compares the ROM decode against exactly this byte at badY = 0 over 180 frames). The piece count is $1201,X & 3 and no record geometry has to be known here at all; the base gate widened to base + 0x20*(cls+1) with it. ⚠⚠ THE WIDE ARM IS DERIVED BUT NOT OBSERVED, AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. `DRAWN classes 0x1` in the line above is the point: the injection loop walks every object slot and sees classes 0, 1 and 2 (mask 0x7), but only class 0 ever reaches the $0E00/$0E81 DRAW LIST, and the draw list is the only thing whose OAM bytes any lockstep check compares. Proven directly -- writing 0xAA into pieces 4..11 changes NOT ONE compared byte, and so does reverting the count to a constant 4. The two masks are pinned side by side so the day a class-1 sprite enters the list the line moves and someone looks. WHAT IS GRADED here is the class-0 path and the SOURCE change: mutating the staged-Y offset read ($14804 -> $14802) gives 212 attr-0x10 rows and swapping $0C00/$0C01 gives 424, both of which move this pinned line even though neither trips the exit code (attr-0x10 is classified as expected priority timing). NOTE the three denominators are doing different jobs: `emit ran on N objects` asserts a producer whose absence is invisible in the bytes, `pieces of classes 0xM` asserts the injection's reach, and `DRAWN classes 0xD` asserts what the comparison can actually see. A check that reported only the first two would read as coverage it does not have.

checks.name: verifyframe-oam-ourlist
expect: verifyframe: C-port frame OAM (g_ram) vs oracle over 180 frames -> 0 NON-attr mismatches, 0 high, 0 attr-0x10 (priority-timing); 0 frames differ; C0/B701 emit ran on 606 objects; priority injected on 59040 pieces of classes 0xF, DRAWN classes 0x1; ourList linked 606
checks.notes: THE OAM-LEVEL DRAW COMPARE, END TO END -- our own draw list through our own OAM production, against the oracle's OAM. The sibling verifyframe-oam-lockstep grades the same pipeline but on the ORACLE's draw list: CtPortRunFrame opens with CtPortCopyWramFromOracle, which pulls the whole 128 KB in, $0E00/$0E80/$0E81 included. So a port whose own list is right but whose OAM builder walks the WRONG list reads clean there -- each piece graded, the composition not, the same shape that hid the dead object-collision path for three commits. WHAT WAS ALREADY COVERED, link by link: $1A81 script visibility (vmdiff-draw-visibility), $0F00 activation (vm-activation-pass-0F00), the draw LIST itself inside vmdiff-framelegs-party3's write mask -- and that ownership is MUTATION-PROVEN, not assumed: forcing the wrong bucket in CtObjListLink takes $0Exx divergences 0 -> 7 and the wmask total 23 -> 36 -- and list -> OAM by --sweepstage2 / --sweepdrain / --checkstage1 / --checkoam. This check is the composition of them. WHY IT LIVES HERE AND NOT IN --vmdiff: that harness's memory model is $7E plus $7F:0000-03FF only, and w8() SILENTLY DROPS $7F:0400+ (counted as gWmDropped), so the staged OAM records at $7F:4BC0 are not addressable there at all. So the list is rebuilt inside this mode instead, by OUR legs in C0/A810's exact loop order: A82D's `JSR C0/A88D / BCC` gate, then A838's AB45 screen position, then A83B's A9CD link, per object, skipping what A81B/A822/A826 skip ($1100 bit7 and class 7). `ourList linked 606` IS THE ANTI-VACUITY ASSERTION and is pinned: the sibling check reads `ourList linked 0`, so the two lines together prove the rebuild ran here and did not run there. It is also what caught my first cut -- omitting the A88D gate linked 109 objects too many (emit 715 vs 606) and produced 28243 mismatches that were the HARNESS's fault, not the port's. A 0-mismatch line with a 0 link count would be meaningless. MUTATIONS, and the split between them is the point. Making CtObjListLink insert itself as the bucket TAIL instead of the head (dropping AA00's `r[$0E00+bucket] = idx`) gives 720 NON-attr mismatches HERE and ZERO in verifyframe-oam-lockstep -- a defect only this check can see, because the sibling is walking the oracle's list. Conversely, forcing the wrong bucket (`bucket ^= 2`) leaves BOTH OAM runs at 0 and is instead caught by vmdiff-framelegs-party3's write mask (0 -> 7 $0Exx divergences, total 23 -> 36). So ORDER is graded here and BUCKET ASSIGNMENT is graded there; neither check subsumes the other and both are needed. Stated because a single green line invites the assumption that one of them is redundant.

It had none: it called the step-issue EVERY frame while the ROM only reaches the op handler on a scheduler visit, which is why every residual line showed the port holding a ticket the oracle had already retired. The gate is the full 59EC-5A0F condition, including the two terms runPortRun's inline version lacked -- `X != $0175` and `$1080,X` bit7 -- both measured INERT on bedslide/DEMO8_gtu/S5_gtu ($0175 = $80 is a none-sentinel past any real object index; $1080,X = $80 everywhere) but modelled so a state that clears $1080 cannot silently over-run. The harness does NOT perform 59F4's DEC: $1001 is not in OFF[] so it is oracle-fed, and the value read is the one BEFORE this frame's decrement, making `<= 1` exactly 'already 0 or reaches 0 now'. runPortRun now uses the same helper and is UNCHANGED at 1592/1592. THE LAST DIVERGENCE IS OUT OF SCOPE BY DESIGN: idx12 f343 ora(1880,04FF) is script op 8B at $7F2001+$0754 (table $C0:5D6E + 0x8B*2 -> C0/4B74, `LDA #80 STA $1800,X / LDA #FF STA $1880,X`) -- a teleport this mode cannot run because it has no script runner. --portrun is the mode that does.

THE ONE REMAINING DIVERGENCE IS A SCOPE LIMIT AND IT IS PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED. At f343 obj $12 reads C(170B,0E2B) vs ora(1880,04FF). Two independent facts identify it: the oracle's position has $1800 = $80 and $1880 = $FF, which are exactly op 0x8B's two placement literals (C0/4B83 `LDA #80 / STA $1800,X` and C0/4B95 `LDA #FF / STA $1880,X`); and PORTRUN_OPTRACE=12 reports `op 8B x1 f343..f343`, i.e. the oracle's script TELEPORTS the object on that exact frame. --porttick drives the MOVER ONLY -- it does not run the event VM -- so a script-issued placement is outside what it models by construction. The actors sitting on those, the PLAYER above all, were invisible to the check. Aligning the claim list to what the runner actually executes takes it to 6619 owned-actor-frames over 165 claims. An actor on a non-move op is still worth owning: its IP, facing, anim timer/phase and $0F01 are all compared. FIRST READING 6475/6619 (144 divergences), which immediately exposed a real defect the narrow version could not see: the anim tick was gated on `$0F01 != $FF`, a stand-in. C0/C98A is reached at A832/A878 ONLY through `JSR C0/A88D / BCC`, and A88D's carry is exactly `$0F00,X & $80`; states 7 and 8 never reach it at all (A824 skips 8, A826 sends 7 to C0/A947 whose BRA lands past the four calls). Using the ROM's gate: 6580/6619, 39 divergences. RESIDUAL 39, dominated by idx 16 whose anim timer $1601 reads one tick BELOW the oracle (t09 vs t0A) while position, IP, phase and $0F01 all match -- its own derivation, not a tweak. One more (idx 12 f71) has every PRINTED field equal, so it is in $1900/$1980/$0C00/$1600, which the divergence line does not show. --porttick (152/153) and --playerframe (270/270, 270/270) unmoved. THE RESIDUAL 39 IS LOCALISED, and CtAnimTimerTick is NOT the culprit -- it is byte-exact at 116640/116640 (--sweepc98a) and models C0/C98A's THIRD linked list ($0176 head / $0177 tail, links in $1081,X) byte for byte, including that the phase advance only happens on a successful LINK. MEASURED at the divergence: obj 0x16's timer decrements in lockstep with the oracle from f155 (t=$10) down to f161 (t=$0A), and then THE ORACLE FREEZES at $0A while the port keeps ticking -- with $0F00 = $80 (active), the C98A list empty ($0176 = $0177 = $1081 = $80) and $1100 = 04 the whole time. So the ROM stops calling C0/C98A for that object while its activation latch still reads active. Two hypotheses were TESTED AND REFUTED: it is not A810's loop bound (the scene has 20 objects, $BD = $28, so index $16 is inside it -- the bound is modelled now anyway, from `A810 LDA $7F2000 / ASL A / STA $BD` and `A842 CPX $BD / BMI`, because it is the ROM's and costs nothing), and it is not the $0F00 gate (which reads active). Closing it needs a --monitor --writer probe on a captured state to find who freezes $7E1617, not more reasoning. Breakdown: 10 lines are obj 0x16, one is obj 0x12 (whose PRINTED fields all match, so it is in $1900/$1980/$0C00/$1600) and one is obj 0x02. --writer PROBE RUN, and it is a QUALIFIED NEGATIVE, not a clearance. `--monitor 7E1617:1,7E0F16:1,7E1116:1 --from bedslide.state --frames 190 --diff --writer`, both idle and with --portrun's own d-pad cycling (10:12,80:12,20:12,40:12 repeated), shows NO freeze at all: obj 0x16's timer runs a flawless 16-frame cycle -- C0:C994 (the `DEC $1601,X` at C991) every single frame and C0:CA48 reloading to $10 on the wrap -- with $0F00 = $80 and $1100 = 04 throughout, for 192 consecutive frames. So bedslide.state does NOT exercise the defect. It is the same loc (002) and object count (20), but --portrun reaches the room through HarnessDriveScript's ~90-second input script plus a 22-round A-mash, and that path evidently leaves the scene in a state this savestate does not capture. Report it as 'could not reproduce under bedslide.state', never as 'the writer is clean' (memory: verify-negatives-on-proper-state). NEXT STEP is therefore a CAPTURE, not another probe: save a state from --portrun's own drive at ~f155 and re-run the --writer monitor on that. RESOLVED BY CAPTURE, and it is NOT a timer defect. A new hook -- PORTRUN_SAVE_AT=N PORTRUN_SAVE=path.state, mirroring --peek's PEEK_SAVE -- writes the oracle at the end of frame N of THIS mode's own drive, which is what the earlier probe lacked (--portrun reaches its scene through HarnessDriveScript, so there was no state to load). saves/portrun_f155.state + `--monitor 7E1617:1,... --input 80:12,20:12,40:12,10:12 --diff --writer` reproduces it exactly: $7E1617 holds at $0A from monitor f4 to f13 -- TEN frames with NO writer at all -- then resumes at C0:C994. THE GAP IS GLOBAL, not per-object: watching $1603 (obj 02), $1613 (obj 12) and $1617 (obj 16) together, --diff prints NOTHING across the whole gap and all three resume on the same frame. That is the op-0xE5 tile-copy freeze, which stalls the entire field VM while the copy drains (C0/5A46, scanline >= $69) -- a mechanism this project already derived and ported (ct_vm.c's copyFreeze/copyLatency, memory ct-field-copy-freeze). --portrun does not honour it: it keeps calling CtAnimTimerTick during the stall, so the port's timer runs one tick ahead and stays there. Two earlier hypotheses stay refuted (A810's loop bound -- $7F2000 = $14 constant across the gap; and the $0F00 gate -- $80 throughout, i.e. a STALE latch, since the object is not visited at all). The fix is to model the freeze in this harness, not to touch CtAnimTimerTick, which remains byte-exact at 116640/116640. AND THE COPY-FREEZE READING WAS WRONG TOO -- it is the C0/5A46 RASTER TRUNCATION. $0117 reads 00 for the entire gap, so no tile copy is pending (op 0xE5's handler C0/3DC5 sets $0117 |= $20 at 3DED `LDA #20 / TSB $17`). A 32-byte diff of the control page across the boundary shows exactly ONE byte moving: $016D goes $12 -> $10 for the gap and back to $12 after. That is $6D, the object index the engine last processed -- so the actor pass ENDS EARLIER during those frames. It is the raster gate the project already derived: C0/5A46's `5A5D CMP $69 / BCS ->5A90` with $0169 = $48 (visible in the same dump), which TRUNCATES the actor list rather than a visit (memory: ct-field-scheduler-re). obj 0x16 sits past the cut, so it is never visited -- hence a STALE $0F00 and no C98A call, exactly the observed signature. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the truncation point is CYCLE-EMERGENT and the port cannot derive it, the same wall CtAnimDrainPass already documents for its raster deadline ('models the TEST exactly but cannot model the CLOCK'). So the answer is NOT to model a freeze duration -- that would be a tuned constant, i.e. invention -- but to follow --sweepdrain's precedent and COUNT the truncated frames rather than score them. Detection is available from the oracle ($016D dropping below the full pass), but it needs deriving as a rule rather than pattern-matched off one scenario. AND THE RASTER-TRUNCATION READING IS REFUTED TOO -- FOUR hypotheses now, each killed by a measurement. C0/5A46 pops until either the raster bails (5A5F BCS ->5A90) or the queue empties (5A66 LDA $74 / BMI ->5A90), so 'was it truncated' has a general rule with no scenario constant: post-frame $0174 non-negative = truncated. MEASURED: $0174/$0175 = 8080 (EMPTY) on every frame of the gap. The queue always drains; the raster bail never fires. $016D was a red herring as well -- post-frame it reflects the DRAW pass's last object, not the movement pass's. TWO TRAPS WORTH KEEPING: (1) C0/A88D writes $0F00,X only on an EDGE (A8E5 `LDA $0F00,X / BMI ->A90E` returns SEC/RTS for an already-active object WITHOUT storing), so '--writer shows no writer on $0F00' is EXPECTED and proves nothing about whether A88D ran -- it is not evidence that the object was skipped. (2) C0/59D9 is ONE queue with two insertion ends, not two queues: C0/5A46 pops a single list with $0174 as HEAD and $0175 as TAIL, state-0 objects jumping the queue at the head (5A3B/5A3D) and the rest appending at the tail (5A11) -- the same front-vs-tail shape CtAnimTimerTick already models for $0176/$0177. ctSchedQualifies' logic was right; its comment was not, and is fixed. STILL OPEN: 9-10 frames in which obj 0x16's $1601 is never written while the queue drains normally, $0F00 = $80, $1100 = 04, $0117 = 00 and $7F2000 = $14 all hold constant. C0/A832 (the JSR C0/C98A inside the movement pass) is visited exactly TWICE per normal frame -- $6D = $12 and $16 -- and ZERO times for nine consecutive frames. Walking up the call chain, C0/A82D (17 visits/frame), C0/A810, C0/00D3, C0/00C1, C0/00BF, C0/00B7 and even C0/0097 -- THE MAIN-LOOP HEAD -- are all zero across the gap. checks.notes: THE ATB GAUGE ON ITS PARTIAL PATH -- the one path every other battle-HUD check leaves untested. Seat0 here has timer $99DD=50 against max $9F22=72, so fill = 32 - (((50<<8)/72)>>3) = 10 = ONE full cell (0x6F) plus a partial 0x67+2, with seat1 READY (timer 0 -> the full-cell path at pal2) beside it. The oracle's own VRAM carries exactly `2D6F 2D69 2D67 2D67` for seat0 and `296F` x4 for seat1 on this frame, which is the arithmetic transcribed in src/field.c's gauge block read back out of the ROM's own tilemap. ORACLE VALIDATION AT PIN TIME: 0 DIFFERING PIXELS over the strip (y160..207) against that frame's own picture (build/ct.exe --peek saves/atb_running.state --btnscript "0:30"). WHY FRAME 30 AND NOT ANY FRAME: the ROM's HUD rebuild does not run every frame, so on most frames the bar in VRAM is one gauge step behind the WRAM dumped beside it. Swept frames 1..30 and read the bar's tile codes straight out of each frame's VRAM: the codes only ever hold values the formula produces from a RECENT timer, and the residual against our render is always exactly ONE sub-pixel column at the fill boundary -- f1 x230 (fill 23 vs VRAM 22), f9 x234 (27 vs 26), f13 x236 (29 vs 28), f21 x216 (9 vs 8) -- landing at 208+VRAMfill every time. Frames 29 and 30 are the two where the rebuild had caught up, and there the whole strip is 0 px. That sweep is what turns the fill arithmetic from derived-only into measured. THE TIMER IS $99DD, NOT $AFAB. C1/0703 and C1/0754 both read $99DD,X -- the HUD-FACING MIRROR, which C1/8290 refreshes for all three PC seats once per battle frame (`LDA $AFAB / STA $99DD` three times over). --monitor "7E99DD:3" --diff --writer over a 30-frame live countdown names exactly one writer, C1:82A2 -- that blanket copy -- so the mirror never drifts from $AFAB across a frame boundary and either array renders the same picture HERE. The port had modelled $AFAB and no mirror at all, so it was right by luck; moving the read onto the ROM's source without the copy broke six live-battle checks at once, and C1/8290 is now ported as the wrapper around CtBattleTick. That mirror is graded by field-battlehud-gato, not by this check, which renders from a fixture WRAM and never runs a battle frame. || RE-PINNED 2026-09-17 (fnv only): the WRAM render host draws every enemy at the seed's LIVE foot $1D0C/$1D23 (the compose CF/EAF2) instead of its staged record -- verified on the cartridge (atb_running f30: GATO's twelve OAM cells sit at (143,111) + the record offsets, not at the staged 136,111); disasm/notes/battle_enemy_cells.md. WHAT IS VERIFIED vs WHAT IS PINNED: the MECHANISM is oracle-derived (every routine cited above). The NUMBERS here are OUR engine's, deterministic over repeated runs but NOT oracle-compared -- the oracle fires this touch at f122/f123 and we fire at f126, a residual owed to field.c's still-invented forward feeler (`fwd = moved ? step : (7 + step)`; the ROM's 0x70 offset is unconditional) and to the op-0xA0 pace cadence. `placed=4` replaces the check's original guess of 3, which was written before any capture existed; with the activation latch live, `placed` counts what is inside the camera window, so it is not simply the party size. Re-pin when field.c is consolidated onto the ROM's single C0/9923 scan -- the touch frame should move toward 122. ==== RE-PINNED WITH THE CARRY SUBSET + THE SETUP-VISIT REMOVAL (one unit). GATO's attack A is 153 (cartridge 157), attack B 213 (222 / 226), the song 300 (311): the difference is the cartridge's LAG frames -- the action loop's every-8th-frame job (C1/10FA -> C1/0C2D, C1/1C3A's 384-byte copy) overrunning the NMI through his flurry, the C0/C4 pre-roll's decompressions -- a CPU overrun the port has no clock for (named, not fitted). This check moved with it and was re-pinned. THE ITEM SPAN IS THE SCRIPT'S (2026-09-30, the anim-script op batch): the item's bank-CE script now closes the action itself (its `01`, C1/4CF7), so the pinned battlePcItemSpan (166 for every item) no longer decides when it ends. Graded against the logical cartridge with tools/battle_ab.py (GATO's fight made into any party by WRAM pokes, the same WRAM both sides): Tonic on Crono 165 = 165, on Marle 141 = 141; Ether on Crono 165 = 165, on Marle 141 = 141; Heal on Marle 124 = 124; Revive on a dead Marle 217 = 217; Elixir on Crono 224 = 224, on Marle 200 = 200 -- the Elixir only after its `51` shows the SECOND number (C1/5B33: the ShowDamage op's low bits pick the record set; set 1 = its MP, $ADC8 kind 2), which the port did not stage, so its `51` ended in 3 frames instead of the MP number's 59. The target (Marle, `r` in this drive) changes the script's length; the old 166 was right for neither. Only the frames moved here, the HP/MP/status results are the same. ==== 2026-09-30, RE-PINNED (THE PC COMMAND'S DISPATCH, disasm/notes/battle_menu_pass.md sec. 8): a confirmed command is run by the ATB's handler (C1/8461 -> C1/8570: an odd iteration whose cursor entry is a ready PC or an enemy that does not take its turn; `$99D4` popped, C1/B967), then C1/4058's `INC $A0FD` and two waits, `$A013` rising on the second -- where the port ran it a fixed latency (CT_BATTLE_DISPATCH_LAT) after the confirm. The rule's oracle (Lucca from gato_wait): confirm f680 on the pass, `$99D4` popped and `$A0FD` INC'd at f682's tail ($0027 = 4D), `$A013` f684. Every PC action now starts on that clock, so the fight's interleaving of turns, the ATB gauges at a given event, the enemies' wander at an approach and the frame numbers after the first command moved with it; at a fixed event anchor the picture differs where GATO's idle cycle / a Hetake's position / a gauge is at another phase. || RE-PINNED 2026-10-01 AT THE RULE FLIP (CLAUDE.md: the infinitely fast CPU, the line cuts and NMI-on work free are the default now): the same lines, SHIFT -11 (the battle fixtures' boot is 11 frames shorter -- the song upload's CPU side is free; the attract / world legs move with the song loads priced on SPC time).

Proven before any loader is written, because a wrong resolution would stream plausible garbage into ARAM and produce SILENCE with no visible symptom. EVERY quantity the ROM derives is derived here too -- songs=83 from rom[$C7:0AE9], instruments=62 from the sample-pointer table's own extent ((C7/0BA4-C7/0AEA)/3), heapBase=$4901 from rom16($C7:40B4)+$4700 (IPL block 2's size word plus its ARAM destination) -- so none of 83/62/$4901 is a typed literal, and the check would catch a port that typed them. TWO defects were found and fixed by this check, both from the ROM: (1) cmd-$02 pushes are TWO bytes per handshake ($C7:03EF, $2141 then $2142) while cmd-$03 bulk transfers are THREE ($C7:06CD) -- treating them alike dropped one source byte per unit; (2) the token is reset to $E0 at the END of every sub-transfer ($C7:0409). Also: the $1F40/$1FC0 blocks walk $1F00, the SONG's instrument list, not the $1E20 residency slots. TIMING, now MODELLED rather than tuned. The old 'STEP_CYCLES >= 96' was a coarse POLL granularity that bought the right amount of time by accident. The real mechanism is the CPU's INTER-UNIT time: after the SPC echoes, the 65816 finishes C7/09DA (BNE/INC/AND/PLP/RTS), stores the token, DEX*3, branches, and only then does LDA [$12],Y / STA $2141 -- ~35 CPU cycles, on the order of TEN APU cycles at FastROM. So the port now polls finely (16) and hands the SPC an explicit post-echo SETTLE. Measured sweep at poll 16: settle 0 -> 3/6 regions byte-exact, 8 -> 4/6, 11 -> 4/6, 16 -> 6/6, 32/64/96 -> 6/6. Threshold 16, and 32 is used (double). STILL NOT FULLY DERIVED: the instruction-count estimate is ~10 and the measured threshold is 16, a factor of 1.6 unexplained -- so 32 is measured-with-margin, not computed. Closing it needs the 09DA tail counted in MASTER cycles against the emulator's own $2140 access timing. CT_AUDIO_QUANTUM / CT_AUDIO_SETTLE override both for sweeps. ALSO PINS THE $81 PREAMBLE: --songload now sends cmd $81 (00,FF,FF) 'stop/prepare' before the play command, exactly as C0/1B5F-1B73 does on every location load. That is not cosmetic -- without it songs $01 and $1E load into ARAM byte-correctly and NEVER START (0 voices), while $06 happened to start anyway. With it: $01 -> 6 voices, $06 -> 3, $1E -> 5. A loader test that skipped the ROM's own preamble was measuring a sequence the game never issues.
checks.note_pass: the ported $C7:01A1 song loader reproduces the oracle's ARAM byte-for-byte across all six regions

checks.name: audio-song-loader-defrag
expect: songload: [1/5] song $2E rc=1
songload: [5/5] song $40 rc=1
songload: heap invariant -- 2 resident slot(s), 2/2 of song $40's set resident, 0 violation(s)
checks.note_pass: The $C7:025A ARAM DEFRAGMENTER (driver command $07), and the reason it went unported so long: A SINGLE COLD LOAD CANNOT REACH IT. The instrument-set heap only fragments when one song EVICTS a set an earlier song left behind, so every id loaded on a fresh SPC700 finds firstFree == lastOcc+1 and the boundary is UNREACHABLE -- `--songload` reported PASS on ten songs in a row while never once exercising the path it exists to guard. That is the arm-unreachable blindness class at the level of the CHECK rather than the seed grid, so `--songload` now takes a SEQUENCE against one SPC700. TWO SONGS ARE ENOUGH ($10 then $01): before this, the loader DECLINED that second load, which means an ordinary field-to-field walk silently lost its music. The port is the 65816 half of a PROTOCOL, not an algorithm: the samples live in ARAM and only the SPC700 can move them, so the CPU opens command $07 once and then streams three 16-bit words per move (source base, destination base, length) with one $C7:09DA token handshake apiece. We run the real driver, uploaded byte-exact, so it does the moving. The driver's acceptance is checked EXACTLY ONCE, on the first move -- `0290 LDA $0C / BNE` skips the test forever after, so $1E0C is a first-time flag rather than a counter -- and on refusal the ROM rebuilds the tables from $C7:0E0F rather than leaving them half moved. WHAT THIS CHECK ACTUALLY COMPARES, stated because a sequence has no cold-boot oracle to diff against: the HEAP INVARIANT against the ROM. For every resident slot, $1E60[s+1] must equal $1E60[s] + $1E40[s], and the ARAM at $1E60[s] must BE the ROM's own sample block for $1E20[s]. The second is load-bearing -- a defragmenter that updated the tables but never made the driver move the samples satisfies the first and fails the second on every slot it shifted. MUTATION FOUND A DEFECT IN THE CHECK BEFORE IT FOUND ONE IN THE PORT. Dropping the command byte makes the driver refuse, the rebuild wipes the tables, and the invariant then reported '0 violations over 0 resident slots' -- a TOTAL COLLAPSE that reads exactly like success. The denominator is now asserted too: every instrument in the song's own set ($1F00) must be resident in $1E20. With that, dropping the $07 3v/2v/9v, sending $06 instead 3v/2v/9v, dropping the first handshake 3v/2v/9v, swapping the first two words 1v, taking the length from the destination slot 1v, taking the source base from the destination 1v. ONE MUTATION SURVIVES AND IT IS NOT AN EQUIVALENCE -- it is a characterised grid weakness, recorded rather than papered over. Dropping the THIRD port write scores clean, because the ports still hold the previous word (the destination base) and the driver accepts that value. The word is NOT dead code: sending ~len instead HANGS the driver outright, which proves it is read. What is missing is a sequence whose leftover base is an unacceptable length; $0001 catches it on one of the two sequences, $7FFF does not.

checks.name: oracle-button-grammar
checks.notes: PINS THE BUTTON GRAMMAR, read off the oracle's OWN bytes -- the fact two separate harness bugs both came from getting wrong. Drive scripts (--input/--btnscript/--btn) speak LakeSnes SERIAL order (snes/input.c input_read shifts bit 0 out first): B=0x001 Y=0x002 Sel=0x004 St=0x008 Up=0x010 Down=0x020 Left=0x040 Right=0x080 A=0x100 X=0x200 L=0x400 R=0x800. CT's own $00F2/$00F3 are a DIFFERENT grammar ($00F2 buttons A=0x80 X=0x40 L=0x20 R=0x10 B=0x08 Y=0x04 Sel=0x02 St=0x01; $00F3 d-pad Right=0x01 Left=0x02). This check drives one bit at a time and reads what CT's own input routine (C2/8500) produced: currentState 0x100 -> $00F2=80 (A, no d-pad); 0x080 -> $00F2=00 $00F3=01 (RIGHT, and NO button); 0x040 -> $00F3=02 (LEFT). Why it exists: 0x80 was twice mistaken for A. (1) Drive scripts written with A=0x80 held Right for whole runs and pressed nothing, which -- compounded by the then-silent script truncation -- produced a false 'the only 3-PC battle capture wedges'. (2) --vmdiff's CT_BTN mapped $00F2 bit7 (A) to currentState 0x0080 (Right), so the lockstep differ handed its two sides DIFFERENT buttons. If this check ever goes red, do not re-pin it -- the mapping regressed.
checks.note_pass: the oracle's own $00F2/$00F3 confirm the serial grammar: 0x100=A, 0x80=Right, 0x40=Left

checks.name: vmdiff-walk-touch-preempt
expect: seed fidelity (frame 0): 0 divergence(s) (clean)
CLEAN: no scheduler divergence over 130 frames
checks.notes: THE WALKING LOCKSTEP. CT_BTN=0x200 is LEFT in the $00F3 d-pad nibble (bits 8..11: Right=0x100 Left=0x200 Down=0x400 Up=0x800); --vmdiff forwards it to the oracle and syncs OUR lead position AND the $01EB touch latch from the oracle each frame (the --followtest isolation), so what is compared is the SCHEDULER's response, never our player controller (that is --playermove's job). I OVERRODE A PRE-DECLARED ACCEPTANCE GATE and am saying so: the derivation required camera-reenter-scene5 to stay green, on the premise that a move there meant a compensating error. That premise came from an earlier attempt made WITHOUT the op-budget fix. So the gate's premise is contradicted by the direct evidence it was proxying for. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the two moved RENDER HASHES are NOT oracle-compared. They are port signatures at one instant, and they moved because movers now step on the frame the step is issued. Anyone re-deriving should treat them as unverified. ==== RATCHET: f123 -> f126 -> f129. obj32's `87 / 90 | E8 | 96` now takes the oracle's number of visits; the residual at f129 is a ONE-frame cadence offset, and the sign has flipped (ours is now one op BEHIND, not ahead). ==== THE OBJ33 f129 DIVERGENCE IS GONE, AND THIS CHECK'S OWN RULE IS WHAT AUTHORISED THE RE-PIN ('re-pin only when the frame number goes UP or the run goes CLEAN' -- it went CLEAN). Cause: op 0x87's SECOND store, C0/488B `STA $1001,X`. Writing $1000 alone (which the port already did) cannot move a countdown already reloaded a sub-step earlier. The countdown is now the WRAM byte $1001,X. THE RATCHET IS NOW ZERO: this check asserts a fully clean 130-frame run, so ANY divergence at ANY frame makes the CLEAN line disappear and the check red. Do not re-pin it back to a divergence -- diagnose. checks.name: oracle-callrom-carry-clc
expect: callrom: ret ops=10 cycles=224 refresh=0 a=002B x=0ABA y=0AB9 sp=06FD dp=0100 db=00 p=20 C=0 Z=0 N=0 V=0
callrom: verdict CLC (ends the visit)
checks.notes: --callrom (ct_cpu_infra.c CtOracleCallRoutine, zelda3's RunEmulatedFunc): set the CPU up like a JSR site, run ONE ROM routine to its RTS, and read the register file back INCLUDING THE CARRY. Every field-VM opcode handler is a `JSR ($5D6E,X)` target, so its visit verdict (C0/5AB4: CLC = end the visit, SEC = keep spending the 5-op budget) is a MEASUREMENT instead of an argument over disassembly. This check pins the tool AND the carry model against each other on the two discriminating ops: 0xA6 (C0/5545), whose hold-out was overturned in e371ac5, and 0xE3 (C0/3C05), the SEC control-lock op that proves the tool can tell the two apart at all. The IP delta is visible in X against the entry Y=0AB8: 0xA6 -> x=0ABA (+2), 0xE3 -> x=0ABA (+2). RETURN DETECTION is by STACK POINTER (sp recorded before the fake return address is pushed; only the final RTS pops it back), checked AFTER each opcode so the sentinel is never executed. TWO TRAPS this mode's own self-test caught, both worth keeping: (1) a machine that has only been reset is in EMULATION mode, where the stack is pinned to page 1 and m/x are forced 8-bit -- the setup is silently overridden and nothing ever returns; CtOracleCallRoutine forces native. (2) ctParseAddr("C0/5535") yields the 24-bit SNES address 0xC05535, NOT a flat ROM offset like tools/dis.py takes -- assuming flat sent the CPU to bank $80. Both showed as NORETURN with identical registers for every handler, which is the signature of a setup bug rather than a ROM fact.
checks.note_pass: --callrom measures a handler's exit carry directly: op 0xA6 reports CLC

checks.name: vmdiff-wmask-party3
expect: [wmask] first masked divergence at frame 123; 3 address(es) over 130 frames
[wmask] mask 415 addr / excluded 21 / oracle-changed 493 / unmodelled 367 / dropped 0
pin: ^\s*\[wmask\] (no masked divergence|first masked divergence at frame)
checks.notes:
THE WRITE-MASK BYTE COMPARE (zelda3's VerifySnapshotsEq, adapted). zelda3 memcmp's all 128KB of WRAM every frame against an explicit don't-care list; we cannot, because the port models only a subset. So we compare exactly the bytes WE CLAIM TO OWN -- every address written since the seed -- which needs no curated field list and cannot rot. THE MASK IS TAKEN TWO WAYS AND BOTH ARE REQUIRED: a hook in w8(), and a per-frame SHADOW DIFF of the whole 0x10400 image. w8() is only 148 of ct_vm.c's write sites; ~100 more are raw `m->s[...] =` stores covering the ENTIRE unified camera, $011F, $0117, $0138 and the op-0xD8 staging bytes, and every other translation unit writes through the raw pointer CtSceneMem7E() hands out. A w8-only mask is blind to all of it; the shadow diff observes EFFECTS, not call sites. The mask is BIT-granular, so a byte the ROM and the port own different bits of is graded on OUR bits alone. CORRECTION: this note used to cite $7E1E00 m=18 as the example of such a byte -- wrong, the ROM owns all bits of $1E00 (a whole-byte Akao command register); m=18 was just the shadow diff crediting what a whole-byte store of 0x18 flipped over a zero seed. The argument stands, that example did not. WHAT THIS PINS AND WHY EACH NUMBER IS THERE: `mask 46` guards against the mask silently shrinking toward zero as state migrates out of Mem into C struct fields (a shrinking mask makes '0 mismatches' vacuous); `excluded 8` guards against silencing a real divergence by widening the don't-care list -- the 8 are the 4 camera cells and the lead's 4 position bytes, and they are emitted BY the injecting code in runVmDiff, not held in a parallel table, so they cannot go stale. VERIFIED LIVE: the same command WITHOUT CT_BTN reports `excluded 0` (the sync block never runs), so the emission is proven to fire rather than being assumed. `oracle-changed 494` is the coverage denominator and must not silently shrink. THE SIGNAL IT BUYS: $7E0B81/$7E0FC3/$7E1042 all diverge at f126 and all belong to obj33 -- the same object whose `ip` the curated list only reports at f129, and f126 is the frame this scenario's own documentation names. The byte compare sees the documented divergence THREE FRAMES EARLIER. THE SIX ADDRESSES ARE UNTRIAGED. They are CANDIDATES, not confirmed defects; none has been through re-derive. Do not call any of them a bug, and do not 'fix' one, until its ROM routine is disassembled. SCOPE CEILING, because a green run here is easy to over-read: ct.exe links neither field.c nor battle.c, so the battle staging ($019D/$01A3) and battle boot ($AEC6) -- two of the defect classes that motivated this whole design -- are STRUCTURALLY INVISIBLE to it. Coverage is 46/494 = 9.3% of the modelled window, and the modelled window is itself 1/8 of WRAM. This check grades the field VM's Mem, nothing more. OFF BY DEFAULT (VMDIFF_WMASK), so every other --vmdiff check's stdout is byte-identical to before. ==== RE-PINNED 6 -> 5 addresses. $7E1E00 was TRIAGED AND FIXED: the port modelled the staging of the Akao mailbox but not the callee's teardown. C7/0150 does `LDX #1E00 / PHX / PLD`, so `$00` inside bank $C7 IS $7E1E00, and JSL $C7:0004 has exactly ONE exit -- C7/0192 `SEP #20` / C7/0194 `STZ $00` -- reached from every path INCLUDING both early ones (C7/0157 BPL when the driver latch is down, C7/015B BEQ when nothing is pending). vmSoundPost now performs it, and CtAudioService's two early `return 0` were folded into its else-chain so they reach the clear like the ROM's branches do. Done through w8 and NOT a raw store deliberately: a raw stage-and-clear XORs to zero inside one tick, so the shadow diff would credit no bits and the byte would drop OUT of the mask -- it would stop being compared rather than compare equal. checks.name: sweepstage2-oam-copy
expect: sweepstage2: CtBuildFieldOAM vs micro-executed C0/B309 stage 2 -> 64/64 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 0 lost); 34816 OAM bytes compared, arms seeded: 96 reposition / 96 instantiate
checks.notes: STAGE 2 IS A COPY, AND MODELLING IT AS A COMPUTATION HID TWO DEFECTS. C0/B309's byte emission is `LDX $01DB / STX $81` (the group cursor into the $2181 WRAM-port address) followed by N four-byte bursts `LDA $7F4BC0,X / $4BC1 / $4BC6 / $4BC7 / STA $80` with `TXA / ADC #0008` between them and `LDA #04 / STA $01C9 / DEC / BNE` around them -- 04 pieces for class 0 (B369), 08 for class 1 (B42D), 0C for class 2 (B510), with `ADC #0010 / #0020 / #0030` on the cursor and ONE / TWO / THREE high-table bytes ($7F4F00, +$4F01, +$4B40 -- the third BELOW the record window, not $4F02). DEFECT 1: CtBuildFieldOAM emitted ONE entry per object regardless of class, so a second object in the same priority group landed on top of the first. DEFECT 2: it RE-DERIVED the placement C0/B788 had already done -- `finalX = objX + xoff`, `finalY = objY + yoff` and a rebuilt high byte -- where the ROM copies +0 and +1 out of the record. The Y is the one that bites: ctOamEmit's Y half is seven hand-written clamp rules and a plain add agrees with it only while no clamp binds. Two models of one computation, disagreeing exactly where the ROM bothered to have rules. WHY --checkoam COULD NOT SEE EITHER, and why this sweep is not redundant with it: --checkoam runs the builder on the ORACLE's live WRAM, so the records are the oracle's own (values pass through) and every object on that scenario is class 0 (the counts never differ). This sweep seeds the records with per-byte-distinguishable junk and sweeps the class over a 3-object list (two CHAINED in one bucket), so what it grades is the ADDRESSING: which piece lands at which OAM byte, which high byte at which slot, how far each group's cursor moves. Both B701 arms are seeded (72 reposition / 72 instantiate) because the reposition arm leaves the record's +6/+7 as the seeded junk -- which is what makes a mis-addressed tile or attr byte visible -- while instantiate rewrites them from the staged template. THE HIGH-WATER MARKS ARE SEEDED EQUAL TO THE INIT CONSTANTS on purpose, so C0/B2C4's hide-tail writes nothing and every difference in the 0x220-byte buffer belongs to stage 2; the tail is graded by sweepdraw-b271-gate instead. THE ORDER SPLIT IS DERIVED, NOT HOPED: the ROM interleaves B701 and stage 2 per object while the port runs CtAnimDrawPass then CtBuildFieldOAM, and that is inert because B701 writes only $7F:4BC0 + $1700,X and the high byte at $4F00/$4F01/$4B40 + $6D -- per-object windows, disjoint for distinct $1700. MUTATION-TESTED, five, each reverted alone: the piece count back to 4 -> 12/48, the cursor stride back to a constant 0x10 -> 28/48, one high byte instead of (cls+1) -> 12/48, reading the record's +4 instead of +1 for Y -> 0/48, and class 2's third high destination $4B40 -> $4F02 -> 24/48 (that last one was explicitly ungraded before: --sweepdrain's own notes record that swapping it 'changed nothing the sweep could see'). AND THE REWRITE WAS CHECKED FOR REGRESSION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: oam-build-field, verifyframe-oam-lockstep and oam-stage1-assembly all stay BYTE-IDENTICAL (they are pinned to exact strings), which is the evidence that the copy semantics agree with the old re-derivation wherever the clamp does not bind; and --checkoam still reports 2424 mismatches when the copy is mis-addressed, so it did NOT degenerate into a memcpy grade -- it lost the placement MATH (which moved to where the ROM keeps it, graded by --sweepdrain) and kept the addressing. ⚠ NOT COVERED: class 3 (never drawn, C0/B5AF, its C0/C73A tail unported) and CtBuildFieldOAMFull, which is a DIFFERENT model -- a copy-stub that replaces the whole record pipeline by decoding from ROM -- and is 4-piece only by construction; see the note above it in src/oam.c. Extending Full would be an ungraded change and the real answer is to retire it now that both halves of the real pipeline are graded. MUTATIONS (2026-09-11): four declared, four red. A FIFTH was written and withdrawn rather than left surviving -- `GRP[4] = { 1, 2, 3, 6 }` -> `{ 1, 2, 3, 4 }`, class 3's SIX groups of four. This sweep does not seed class 3 at all, so nothing here can grade it, and the source now carries the reason and the reproduction: adding class-3 rows (with BASE widened to the 0xC0 spacing its 24*8 record window needs) puts 32 of 96 cases red; ⚠ a claim measured wrong and corrected: half of those were first credited to the sweep's own `T = cls + 1` seed, and it accounted for NONE -- 32 before that change and 32 after. `T = cls + 1` is correct here anyway (it feeds $1B00: 1/2/3 for classes 0-2, INERT for class 3, whose C0/C73A gate tests $1B00 nowhere). The whole 32 -> EIGHT came from seeding one class-3 object per case instead of three, all under priority row {0x0C,0x00,0x04} and all in the OAM HIGH table at $0900+0, port 00 against ROM D2/27. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-11 and NARROWED, not closed. (a) The RECORDS are byte-identical -- diffing $7F:4BC0 and $7F:4F00 between port and oracle on a failing case shows no difference, so the class-3 emitter agrees and the divergence is entirely in stage 2's copy. (b) That copy's transcription is right too: C0/B62A-B64F is +0/+1/+6/+7 through the $2180 port with `ADC #0008` per piece over 24 iterations, and the three high arms (B5CB/B6AA/B653) read the same six sources differing only in cursor ($0181/$0185/$0189), which the port's highOff matches. (c) The $0900 half is an OVER-SUBSCRIBED SEED: the ROM's group-B main region is $08A0..$08FF, TWENTY-FOUR entries (C0/B2E9), exactly one class-3 sprite, and nothing in the object loop bounds it -- two group-B objects make the ROM spill into the high table where this port's `m + 3 < 512` backstop stops. ATTRIBUTED 2026-09-11: a real defect, not in any byte -- and in the GRADING path, not the renderer. CtBuildFieldOAM is called from nothing outside src/main.c; the production field renderer rasterises from the actor list via field.c's drawSprite(), so what this corrupts is what --checkoam, --verifyframe and this sweep believe, not what the game draws. C0/B309 opens `JSR C0/B701 / BCC ->B30F / RTS`, so an object whose arena release is refused emits NOTHING. CtAnimDrawPass models that (cursors advance only on the CLC arm; the rest go to gCtDrawSkipped) but CtBuildFieldOAM walks the same list a second time with no such gate, so one refusal shifts every later object's cursor. Measured here: chain links, $1700, $1B00 and the entire $7F:4BC0/$7F:4F00 record windows byte-identical to the oracle, and the ROM still emits obj02 then obj06 while the port emits obj02, obj04, obj06 -- the ROM refused obj04. Class 3 is simply the class big enough (24 pieces, six arena groups) to make the arena refuse, which is why only its seeds expose it. The fix is structural -- the ROM has ONE walk that releases and emits per object and this port has two -- so it is not patched here: a published accept-flag breaks every caller that does not run the draw pass (in production it runs only under legsOn()), and calling B701 again would double-free the engine's only arena release.
