checks.name: sweepcb3a-frame-lookup
expect: sweepcb3a: CtFieldFrameLookup vs micro-executed C0/CB3A -> 2187/2187 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 65 mode2-noncommit, 0 lost)
checks.notes: Sweeps CtFieldFrameLookup (the port's C0/CB3A, the animation ROW SELECT) against a MICRO-EXECUTION of the real routine over a synthetic cross-product of its inputs -- same shape as --sweepactor. It exists because the field it grades was ALREADY compared and still went unguarded: --porttick's match conjunction includes cram[0x0F01+idx] == r[0x0F01+idx] (src/main.c), yet it stayed 128/136 across two real defects, because its tracked scenario never reaches an owned object in the states that trigger them. Driving the inputs directly is what makes them visible. IT CATCHES BOTH DEFECTS IT WAS BUILT FOR -- verified by reverting each and watching it go red: revert the facing-1 row (C0/CB43's BPL tests the sign of (A-2), not of A, so facing 1 takes the x1 row) -> 668 mismatches; revert the sentinel WRAP (C0/CBC8-CBDA rewinds $D6 by $D9 = the phase, marks $1681 = 0xFF, RE-FETCHES and returns SEC, where the port returned 0xFF and main.c's `fb != 0xFF` gate then skipped the commit) -> 148; both in place -> 0. THE 86 mode2-noncommit ARE NOW JUDGED, not excused (they were unported when this check landed). Carry-clear is the mode-2 repeat path (C0/CBA4-CBB0 `LDA $7F0B01,X / DEC A / ... / CLC / RTS`) -- the ROM declining to commit the frame. The port cannot express that: move.c:140 explicitly defers the cfg==2 ping-pong and the function returns a byte with no commit signal. Scoring them as mismatches would judge it against a contract it does not have. They carry their own pinned number so that PORTING the repeat path moves it and this check notices. The cfg==3 short-circuit is excluded for the same reason -- it lives in CB3A's CALLER (C0/CBF2-CBF9), not in CB3A. The facing alphabet deliberately includes values ABOVE 3 (4, 0x7F, 0x80, 0x81, 0xFF): op 0xA6 stores its operand RAW with no &3, so $1600 can hold anything, and the (A-2) rule and a bit7-of-A rule disagree there too. ==== RE-PINNED 2101 -> 2187: the mode-2 REPEAT path is ported, so the sweep no longer skips its own carry-clear cases -- it now compares the whole input space including the commit decision, the $1681 phase writeback AND the $7F0B01 repeat-state writeback. C0/CBA4-CBB0: on the sentinel the cfg==2 arm decrements $7F0B01,X (leaving it when the DEC would hit 0) and returns CLC, where the cfg!=2 arm rewinds and re-fetches -- CB8B `BNE ->CBB1` splits them, and the first cut of the wrap fix wrongly applied the rewind to every cfg. CtFieldFrameLookup now returns -1 for 'do not commit' and main.c's gate is `fb >= 0`; the old `fb != 0xFF` ALSO swallowed a wrap whose re-fetched frame happened to be 0xFF. Acceptance re-verified by reverting the new arm: 86 mismatches, restored 0. SCOPE, stated because it is easy to over-read: this check covers CtFieldFrameLookup ONLY. The other half of the mode-2 work -- CtAnimTimerTick's ping-pong (C0/CA4F-CA69: v==1 -> DEC $1681 with v untouched; v==2 -> v:=1 then DEC $1681; else v-=2 and phase:=0, the sequence REVERSING at its sentinel instead of restarting) -- is ported but UNGRADED. --porttick (128/136) and --portrun (1592/1592) are unchanged with it in, for the same reason they were unchanged for the facing fix: their scenarios never reach a mode-2 object. ==== THAT GAP IS NOW CLOSED by sweepc98a-anim-timer, which micro-executes C0/C98A the same way; reverting the ping-pong turns it red at 2856. --porttick and --portrun remain 128/136 and 1592/1592, confirming again that neither can see this.

checks.name: sweepc98a-anim-timer
expect: sweepc98a: CtAnimTimerTick vs micro-executed C0/C98A -> 174960/174960 byte-exact (0 mismatch: 0 anim-state, 0 queue, 0 lost)
checks.notes: Sweeps CtAnimTimerTick (the port's C0/C98A) against a MICRO-EXECUTION of the real routine over a 116640-combination cross-product of its inputs -- same shape as --sweepcb3a, and built to answer the scope caveat that check left open: the mode-2 ping-pong was ported with NOTHING able to grade it. WHAT C0/C98A ACTUALLY IS -- two routines welded together, and this check grades both. (1) C98A-CA06, the ENQUEUE. $76 and $77 are the head and tail of a singly-linked FIFO of objects waiting on the sprite assembler; the next-pointer is $1081,X and the null is any value >= $80. C0/CA76 pops from the head under a RASTER budget (CAA2-CAD3: pop one, or when head == tail empty the list by nulling both ends), so an object can still be queued when its timer next fires -- and the phase INC lives on the ACCEPT paths only. The animation therefore advances at the rate the assembler drains, not at the rate the timer fires. $1100,X picks the end: >= 3 appends at the tail (C9A6), == 0 pushes at the head (C9D0), == 1/2 appends too (C9E2) unless the one-shot $78 == 2 sends it to the front and clears itself; bit7 is the only state that never enqueues. (2) CA09-CA75, the RELOAD: mod*4 + $1580 + phase indexes a byte in bank $E4; non-zero becomes the new timer, zero means end-of-row -> re-look-up at the phaseless base and reset (or, in mode 2, REVERSE) the phase. THREE DEFECTS FOUND, each acceptance-verified by reverting it alone and watching this check go red. (a) THE ENQUEUE WAS A FLAT GATE -- `st == 0 || st == 1 || st == 2 -> return, no advance` -- which is two errors at once: those states DO advance (via C9D0/C9E2), and state >= 3 does NOT advance when the object is already queued (C9A6's `CPX $77` and C9AE's `LDA $1081,X / BPL`). Revert -> 48564 mismatches (33744 anim-state, 41472 queue). (b) THE CA23 -> CA2E CARRY. `CLC / ADC $1580,X / STA $C1 / <phase> / ADC $C1` -- the second ADC has NO CLC in front of it, so the 16-bit carry out of the first lands in the table index. Revert -> 3024. (c) THE MODE-2 PING-PONG (CA4F-CA69), the one this check was built for. Revert -> 2856. WHY THE FLAT GATE SURVIVED SO LONG, stated because it is the interesting part: in the regime where the drain KEEPS UP -- queue empty at every timer fire -- the flat gate happens to be right for state >= 3, which is the only state the tracked scenarios reach. It is wrong exactly under raster pressure and for states 0/1/2. A scenario check cannot manufacture either; driving the inputs directly can. SCOPE CEILING. CtAnimTimerTick is called from the HARNESSES only (--porttick, and now this) -- src/field.c does not call it, so this grades a ported ROM routine, NOT shipped engine behaviour, and porting the enqueue could not jam the live engine because the live engine does not run it. The queue's DRAIN (C0/CA76 -> C0/CAD9, the sprite assembler) is still unported; only its bookkeeping is derived here, from reading it. --porttick 128/136 and --portrun 1592/1592 are UNCHANGED by all three fixes.
checks.note_pass: CtAnimTimerTick is byte-exact against a micro-executed C0/C98A over 116640 input combinations, enqueue and reload both

WHAT IT IS: a 64-entry WORD table at $C0:9FF7 indexed from the two velocity deltas, dispatching to 8 CARDINAL handlers (stride $0A, unconditional facing), 8 DIAGONAL handlers (stride $15, keep the current facing when it is already one of the diagonal's two components else force the first), and a $9FF2 default that BRLs to the idle chain at C0/A1E9. Two tails: C0/A171 WALK (mode 1) and C0/A18C RUN (mode 6, or mode $17 -- the run-into-wall HEAD-SHAKE -- when velocity, object identity and $E5 are all clear). Every tail ends in the same CMP-guarded 15-byte body, and THE GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING: an unchanged mode resets NEITHER phase nor timer, which is why a held direction does not stutter. WHY IT EXISTS. The routine was ported once WITHOUT a sweep (3648128), wired straight into --portrun on the theory that it drove $0F01, measured at 105 live invocations with the score UNMOVED, and reverted. --portrun could never have graded it: it reaches one facing sequence on one actor, leaving 15 of the 17 slots and every early arm untouched. Driving the inputs directly is what made the defects visible. THE DEFECT THE FIRST CUT HAD, which no scenario had been able to name: the WALK tail C0/A171 opens `STZ $58 / STZ $59` exactly like the RUN tail C0/A18C, and only A18C's copy had been transcribed -- so every seeded idle counter survived a walk. Reverting it alone costs 1280 of 22400. THE SLOT HISTOGRAM IS PART OF THE CHECK, not decoration. The first seed grid reached only 16 of the 17 distinct targets and still reported a clean 14336/14336. The hole was C0/A0B5 (facing 0, RUN tail), which the table holds at X = $40 and NOWHERE ELSE, unreachable while every seeded Y delta folded below it (ix = (fold(dy) | fold(dx)>>3) & $7E). Deltas $40 and $C0 close it. The mode PRINTS a WARNING when distinct < 17 so a future seed change cannot silently re-blind it. The sweep drives all three arms of the 9E88/9E8D branch and grades their effects, so the BEHAVIOUR is pinned even though the MEANING is not. Full derivation: disasm/notes/player_anim_9e84.md.

checks.notes: Fifth of the micro-execution sweep family. Grades VM op 0x02 -- C0/5FB6, the PRIORITY CALL, the ONLY opcode in the ported set that writes ANOTHER object's state. That property is what made --portrun's idx-12 f71 line unreadable for so long: a PORTRUN_HOOKW probe on $1192 named C0/6027 as the writer with `$6D = 10` -- object $10 reaching into object $12's script pointer. No amount of reading object $12's own script could explain an IP that object $12 never moved. THE MECHANISM. Three bytes. Operand 1 is the target object; operand 2 is cleanly `newPrio:slot`, HIGH nibble and LOW nibble. Three reject gates ($1C01,X != 0 / $1100,X bit7 / $1000,X bit7) all branch to 6039, which is the normal exit with one extra INY to make up for the 5FD7 INY they skipped -- so EVERY arm exits IP+3 with carry SET. $7F0580 is a per-PRIORITY-LEVEL array of 128-byte rows indexed by object, addressed via the hardware multiplier (x128). newPrio == cur: nothing at all. newPrio < cur (MORE urgent) = the CALL: save the target's live $1180 at its CURRENT level, load $1180 from the object's fn table at $7F2001 + idx*16 + slot*2, set $1C00 = newPrio, and STZ $1A80/$1A01 to drop any in-flight move. newPrio > cur = the DEFER: PARK the function ENTRY (not a saved IP) at that level, and ONLY if the slot is empty (6053/6057 `LDA $7F0580,X / BNE ->6078` drops the call on the floor); it touches neither $1180 nor $1C00 nor the mover. ⚠ WHY THIS IS A SWEEP AND NOT A --portrun LINE, and why the f71 divergence DID NOT CLOSE: --portrun cannot reach this opcode at all. The actor that executes it there is object $10, and the port DROPS object $10 at f66 on an unported op 0x91 -- FIVE FRAMES BEFORE the call at f71 -- so a --portrun run dispatches op 0x02 exactly ZERO times (measured with a temporary counter) and scores 6462/6466 identically with the handler present or absent. Closing f71 needs op 0x91, not op 0x02. Grading this in --portrun would have been grading nothing, which is the failure this project has now hit four times (--porttick on a harness stub, --playerframe on a memcpy, C0/9E84 on one facing sequence, and this). THE DEFECT THE SWEEP CAUGHT, which careful reading had already missed: newPrio is `LSR A` x FOUR (5FDF-5FE2), not three. Two dis.py windows overlapped at 5FDF and the count came out one short, putting every priority off by a factor of two. First run 699/840. ACCEPTANCE-VERIFIED, ten mutations, each reverted ALONE and each confirmed to go red: the >>3 shift 960/1080; dropping the $1C01 gate 972; dropping the $1000 gate 972; the DEFER arm ignoring the occupied-slot test 990; the CALL saving at the NEW level instead of the current one 972; the CALL forgetting to clear the mover 972; `AND #001F` instead of `#000F` 1038; an idx*8 fn-table stride 1038... (idx*8) 972; the equal-priority arm calling anyway 1038; returning IP+2 1080->810. The three reject gates are seeded ISOLATED (0 = none, 1 = $1C01, 2 = $1100, 3 = $1000) so a port that checks only one of the three cannot pass, and the printed arm histogram fails loudly if any of the four arms is never exercised. PARTNER NOT PORTED: op 0x00 (C0/5F74) is the matching RETURN -- it clears its own $7F0580 slot, then walks DOWN in urgency incrementing $1C00,X until it finds a non-zero slot and returns that as the new IP, with priority 7 meaning 'nothing to return to' (TYX / CLC / RTS, IP unchanged). It is fully derived (note the dead `LDX $6D` at 5FAC, immediately overwritten by TAX -- X IS the handler's return value, exactly like the TYX in every other handler) but deliberately NOT ported here: nothing reaches it either, and porting a second ungraded opcode to keep the first company is how ungraded code accumulates.

checks.name: sweepa88d-activation-gate
expect: sweepa88d: CtObjActiveGate vs micro-executed C0/A88D -> 29040/29040 byte-exact on the carry, the $01C3-$01C6 window and the $0F00 latch (0 mismatch, 0 lost)
verdicts: 4336 active, 24704 inactive
checks.note_pass: CtObjActiveGate is byte-exact against a micro-executed C0/A88D over 29040 combinations, both verdicts produced
checks.notes: Sixth of the micro-execution sweep family. Grades C0/A88D, the OBJECT ACTIVATION GATE -- and the headline fact is that A88D is a RECOMPUTED PREDICATE, not a stored flag. Both arms of C0/A810 reach it (A82D for state >= 3, A873 for state < 3) and both do `BCC` to skip C0/C98A, C0/A98A, C0/AB45 and C0/A9CD; only state 7 (-> C0/A947) and state 8 bypass it. THE PREDICATE: state bit7 clear, $1A81,X in 1..$7F (the byte op 0x90/0x91 writes), and the object's $1801/$1881 -- DOUBLED by an EIGHT-bit ASL, so bit 7 falls off -- inside the camera window $C3 = sat($1D0A-4), $C4 = sat($1D0C+4), $C5 = sat($1D0E-2), $C6 = sat($1D10+5). The two axes do NOT share a margin. THE LATCH IS A PURE FUNCTION OF THE PREDICATE, no hysteresis: A8E5's `BMI ->A90E` only skips the one-shot SETUP for an already-active object and A913's `BPL ->A934` only skips the STZ for an already-inactive one, so $0F00,X ends at $80 or $00 either way. WHAT IS COMPARED and what is not: the CARRY (the routine's whole product), $01C3-$01C6 and the latch. The port stops at the predicate, so the rising-edge one-shot (A8EA-A904), the four sub-calls and the falling-edge tails (A924-A932, A934-A93C) are excluded and NAMED. $0154 BIT 7 IS SEEDED SET, which is the difference between a sweep and a sweep that averts its eyes: C0/7170 and C0/734C -- the OBJ palette assign/release A88D calls on its two edges -- BOTH open `LDA $54 / BMI ->exit`, so the bit makes them inert BY THE ROM'S OWN GATE while the oracle still executes the whole routine. The palette half is ported in ct_vm.c (disasm/notes/objpal_allocator.md). $01C5 IS COMPARED ONLY ON THE INACTIVE VERDICT, for a real ROM reason rather than convenience: C0/A9CD, the list link called on the ACTIVATE edge, reuses $C5 as scratch (`A9F2 STY $C5` ... `A9FD LDY $C5`) and does not restore the byte. The 24704 inactive cases still grade the $1D0E-2 clamp fully. Found by the first sweep run at 8637/8640 -- three mismatches, all on activations. ⭐ THE SEED GRID ITSELF WAS CAUGHT BLIND, and this is the reason the acceptance pass exists. Relaxing the exclusive bound (`>= c4` to `> c4`) left the score at a PERFECT 8640/8640, because a doubled position is always EVEN and no seed ever landed exactly on an edge -- so the BCS-vs-BCC boundary was ungraded. Positions $0F/$1E/$2C/$33/$42 were added to hit tx == c3, ty == c5, tx == c4 and ty == c6 exactly, and one camera row's $1D10 was made ODD so that c6 is EVEN and reachable at all. The mutation then goes red at 28880/29040. ACCEPTANCE-VERIFIED, twelve mutations, each reverted ALONE and each confirmed red: the $1100 bit7 reject 24200; the $1A81 == 0 reject 24200; the $1A81 bit7 reject 24200; -4 -> -0 on the left edge 21296; -2 -> -4 on the top edge 24768; +5 -> +4 on the bottom 23232; a wrapping instead of saturating left edge 25168 and right edge 25168; an untruncated ASL 28288; an undoubled position 27824; inclusive bounds 28880; and writing the window bytes before the flag rejects 9680. NOTE THE DUPLICATION, deliberately not collapsed: ct_vm.c carries an equivalent predicate for the live VM (graded by vm-activation-pass-0F00). The two cannot share code today because that one reads position from sc->fx[] FLOATS rather than $1801/$1881 -- the same split already pinned by vmdiff-withpos-bedslide. Collapsing them is blocked on that, not on appetite.

mutations.why: A897 is `BEQ ->A910` and A899 `BMI ->A910` -- TWO tests on $1A81,X, the byte op 0x90/0x91 writes. Zero means never shown and bit7 means hidden; dropping the zero test activates an object that has never been placed.

mutations.why: the camera window's right margin is FOUR tiles (A8AB `ADC #04`) while the top is two and the bottom five -- the four edges carry different literals and are not interchangeable.

mutations.why: each edge SATURATES: A8B7's `SBC #02 / BCS` re-loads a literal 0 rather than letting the byte wrap. Wrapping turns a camera near the top of the map into a window that excludes everything.

mutations.why: A8D5 is `CMP $C4 / BCS` -- an object exactly ON the right edge is OUT. One boundary pixel, on every object, every frame.

checks.name: sweeptouch-player-redirect
expect: sweeptouch: C0/5B8D gate 256/256 + CtVmTouchRedirect vs micro-executed C0/3154 -> 216/216 byte-exact incl. the whole $7F0580 page (0 mismatch, 0 lost)
arms exercised: redirect 36, skipped 180
checks.note_pass: the touch gate C0/5B8D (all 256 latch values) and the redirect C0/3154 are byte-exact against micro-execution, both arms exercised
checks.notes: Seventh of the micro-execution sweep family. Grades the PLAYER'S TOUCH REDIRECT -- the mechanism that lets a walking NPC's script never have to end, because the encounter is not reached by that script's own closed loop, it is PREEMPTED into it from outside. op 0xB0's state-0 arm ends `304A LDX $6D / 304C LDA $1600,X / 304F JSR C0/5B8D / 3052 BCC / 3054 JSR C0/3154`. C0/5B8D IS TWO INSTRUCTIONS: `LDA $EB / BPL ->SEC ; else CLC` -- carry SET iff $01EB bit 7 is CLEAR, i.e. the touch latch holds a real object index rather than the $80 'nothing' sentinel that C0/881E re-arms every frame. All 256 latch values are swept. NOTE the `304C LDA $1600,X` before the JSR is DEAD -- 5B8D's first instruction overwrites A. (Third instance of this pattern in the field VM, after the dead `LDX $6D` before TAX in op 0x00 and the dead `CMP #$18` before the BRL in C0/9E84.) C0/3154 IS OP 0x02'S CALL ARM WITH TWO CONSTANTS BURNED IN: the target comes from $01EB (whoever the proximity scan hit) instead of a script operand, and BOTH the new priority and the function slot are fixed at 2 (`3190 ADC #0004` = slot*2). Its guard `LDA $1C00,X / CMP #03 / BCC` is op 0x02's `newp < cur` specialised to newp = 2 -- the same law, not a different one. It writes FIVE bytes on the touched object ($1180/$1181, $1C00 = 2, $1A80 = 0, $1A01 = 0 and -- easy to miss at 31AA -- $1001 = 0, the SCHEDULER DELAY, so the preempted object runs on the very next pass rather than waiting out its cadence) plus the $7F0580 save at (curPrio*128 + idx). $0154 BIT 1 IS SEEDED SET so C0/31B1 -- the tail 31AD calls on BOTH non-reject paths, a tile-based shove through $7E7040 with four facing arms, NOT ported -- exits at once through its own `BIT #02 / BNE ->31BB`. Same discipline as --sweepa88d's bit 7 for the palette: the oracle executes the whole routine and simply has nothing to do. The three reject gates are seeded ISOLATED so a port checking only one cannot pass. ⚠ IT DOES NOT MOVE --portrun, and the reason is measured. Probing $01EB across all 360 frames shows the latch DOES fire (`f254 $01EB 80->16 @ C0/9960`) but is re-armed later in the same frame (`12->80 @ C0/993E`) -- the 'last scan wins' semantics collision.c already documents, since the eight directional callers in C0/8A6D-C0/90BF each re-enter the scan. More importantly the redirect targets the TOUCHED object, not the player, and the thing --portrun's idx-16 f254 line actually needs is the PLAYER'S OWN script, which the oracle runs at IP $0445/$0452 and which contains the op 0x0A despawn. THE PORT NEVER OWNS THE PLAYER BEFORE f254: PORTRUN_CLAIMS shows exactly one claim, `idx 02 f254 op B0 ip 0408`, because the claim list only takes an actor whose CURRENT opcode the runner can execute and the player spends f0-f253 in script it cannot. That is a coverage fact worth knowing on its own -- --portrun's player grading starts at f254.

mutations.find: if (cur < 3) return;                                 // 3168 CMP #03 / 316A BCC ->31AD: too urgent
mutations.replace: if (cur < 2) return;                                 // 3168 CMP #03 / 316A BCC ->31AD: too urgent
mutations.why: 3168's `CMP #03 / BCC ->31AD`: an object already running at priority 2 or better is TOO URGENT to be preempted down to level 2. Lowering the bar lets a touch interrupt work that outranks it.

mutations.replace: int sav = 0x10580 + ((cur * 64 + t) & 0xFFFF);
mutations.why: 316C-317E's hardware multiply is a x128 -- $7F0580 is a per-LEVEL save array of 128 objects. A x64 stride makes two priority levels share one region and overwrite each other's saved scripts.
3189-3190 is `ASL A` four times then `ADC #0004` -- sixteen bytes of function table per object, and the touch handler is SLOT 2. Slot 1 is the activate handler; they are different scripts.
319F stores priority 2. The value is what the 3168 gate above compares against on the next touch, so a wrong one makes the preempt either permanent or self-cancelling.

mutations.find: r[0x1001 + t] = 0;                                   // 31AA STZ $1001,X -- the SCHEDULER DELAY, so
mutations.replace: (void)0;                                   // 31AA STZ $1001,X -- the SCHEDULER DELAY, so
mutations.why: 31AA's `STZ $1001,X` clears the SCHEDULER DELAY so the preempted object runs on the very next pass instead of waiting out its cadence. Without it the redirect lands frames late.

checks.name: sweepact-invoke-prologue-guards
expect: sweepact: CtVmInvokeGate vs micro-executed C0/5AC5 + C0/3154 -> 324/324 verdicts exact over the whole 128KB accept/decline image (0 mismatch, 0 lost)
accepted 63 (activate 36, touch 27), declined 261 | accepts per arm: clean 21, $1C01 0/0, $1100 0/0/21, $1000 0/0/21
checks.note_pass: the invoke prologue (C0/5AC5 activate #02 and C0/3154 touch #03) answers exactly as the ROM does, each guard isolated, with the bit7-not-nonzero controls green
checks.notes:
THE INVOKE PROLOGUE, AND IT IS ONE ROUTINE WEARING TWO IMMEDIATES. The ROM's activate invoke C0/5AC5 and its touch invoke C0/3154 are the same seven instructions:
  0x3154  [24 ROM bytes at 0x3154: python tools/dis.py 0x3154 24]
  0x5AC5  [24 ROM bytes at 0x5AC5: python tools/dis.py 0x5AC5 24]
i.e. LDX $EB, then
  LDA $1C01,X / BNE   -- a pending cross-object wait (op 0x08 sets it, op 0x09 clears it)
  LDA $1100,X / BMI   -- DEACTIVATED (op 0x0A, C0/6254: $1100,X := $80)
  LDA $1000,X / BMI   -- PAUSED      (op 0x0B, C0/6269: $1000,X |= $80)
  LDA $1C00,X / CMP #imm / BCC        -- #02 for the activate, #03 for the touch
The port had them in two different shapes: CtSceneActivate carried ONLY the priority test, and CtSceneTouch carried all four but in its own inline copy. Both also AND-ed the priority test with an extra `st->addr >= 0` the ROM does not have -- fail-open, so the port could accept where the ROM declines. They are now one predicate, CtVmInvokeGate(w, obj, prio, minPrio), called by both.
WHY THE MISSING GUARDS MATTER, in order: the PAUSE is the load-bearing one, because the object probe C0/1CFC tests $0F00,X (1D1C) and $1100,X (1D2D) but NEVER $1000,X -- a paused object is a probe hit that only this prologue can refuse, and C0/A88D (the activation pass) tests $1100,X and $1A81,X only, so a paused object stays drawn and stays probe-visible. Decoding all 512 scene scripts (assets/script.py op_len walk from every object's every fn pointer) counts 521 op-0x0B sites and 823 op-0x0A sites.
WHY THE SWEEP COMPARES A VERDICT AND NOT A WRITE SET: a declined invoke writes nothing at all, so 'the whole 128 KB image changed' IS 'accepted' -- there is no hand-listed write set here to be wrong about (the seed poisons $1A80/$1A01/$1001 and $1180 so an accept can never be invisible, and $0154 bit1 is seeded BEFORE the snapshot, or iteration 0 reads its own store as a ROM write -- which is exactly the false mismatch this check reported the first time it ran both entries). The port side is CtVmInvokeGate, the SAME function CtSceneActivate and CtSceneTouch call, so this does not grade a private second copy of the rule.
$1C00,X IS SEEDED ON BOTH SIDES ON PURPOSE. This engine does not maintain that byte: ct_vm.c reads it only to seed (`w[0x1C00 + x] & 0x07`) and never writes it, and a fresh `--scene 2` run dumped at f200 (CT_DUMPWRAM) has $1C00 = 00 for all 24 objects -- a literal `LDA $1C00,X / CMP #02` port would have declined EVERY activate in the game. The live priority is st->prio (7 when idle), and --vmdiff already compares it against the oracle's $1C00 field by field; the sweep hands the ROM the same number it hands the port, which is exactly the equivalence being claimed.
THE ARM COUNTS ARE IN THE PIN and they are what makes 324/324 mean something. 'accepted 63 (activate 36, touch 27)' is the two immediates doing their job: per gate arm and per object, the activate accepts CUR in {02,03,07,0F} (4 of 6) and the touch only {03,07,0F} (3 of 6), so 3 objects x 3 passing arms x 4 = 36 and x 3 = 27. The three passing arms are 'clean' and the two CONTROLS: $1100 = 0x7F and $1000 = 0x7F have every low bit set and must NOT gate -- that is what pins the test to bit7 rather than to 'nonzero'.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT GRADE, stated plainly: the WIRING. Bypassing the gate entirely (`return 1;`) left all 273 other checks GREEN -- measured, not assumed -- because a re-entered fn1 immediately re-parks on the same textbox op ($0129 != 0) and the scene converges. The gate is nevertheless live in real play: instrumented, the scene-8 A-mash (`--scene 8 --walkscript a:3 x100`) takes 15 declines, every one of them the priority arm (obj10 prio=1, Taban already running his own activate response). So the rule is pinned here and the call site is pinned by nothing -- recorded rather than papered over.
OPEN, and deliberately not closed here: this engine has no op-0x08/0x09 handler (C0/6240 `LDX $6D / LDA #01 / STA $1C01,X` and C0/624B `LDA #00`, the only two writers of $1C01 in the whole 4 MB image), so guard 1 is structurally zero on a cold-loaded scene and can only fire on a WRAM-seeded one (savestate, --vmdiff). Adding the two writers without also porting the $1C01 test into the live CALL family (ops 0x02/0x03/0x04, whose ROM sites C0/5FC3 / C0/608B / C0/6127 all carry it, and where 0x02 SKIPs while 0x03/0x04 PARK) would half-wire the mechanism, so it is left whole for its own derivation.

The line under test (5BC3, the CANDIDATE's $0F00) was ungraded: reverting it to the retired `draw` test survived the entire suite, 182/0/0. A divergence counter inside npcSolidTile plus a run over ALL 512 field scenes found exactly THREE that could tell the two apart -- scene 285 (5 of 5 destination-tile candidates decided differently), 294 (3/3) and 298 (25/25) -- and the actor-position hash moved on all three, so a scenario check was genuinely available. Then porting 5B99, the MOVER's own $0F00 which the port was missing, took that to ZERO scenes out of 512: a mover that is itself activated is on-camera, and so is everything near it. THE FAITHFUL PORT MAKES THE LINE UNREACHABLE BY REAL DATA. Keeping the port less faithful to preserve a test would be backwards, so the coverage moved to where it can exist -- exactly the reasoning that produced --sweepowregion. GRADED: six gates against the ROM's own carry. 5B99 mover $0F00; 5BA0 mover $1C80 bit1; 5BC3 cand $0F00; 5BD5 cand $1100 bit7; 5BD7 cand == mover; 5BDB cand $1B01 bit0. The port side is CtVmSolidMoverGate/CtVmSolidCandGate -- THE SAME FUNCTIONS npcSolidTile CALLS, not a copy, because a sweep that grades a private copy grades the copy (that is precisely how the draw compare's class guard survived its own mutation in the commit before this one). Geometry is held constant and passing (candidate 8 px along the heading, inside the ROM's 16 px box on every arm) so a gate verdict is never silently a geometry verdict. ANTI-BLINDNESS IS ASSERTED IN THE OUTPUT: $1A81 is seeded as the exact INVERSE of $0F00 on 192 seeds, so a test reading the script-visibility byte flips on every one of them; and the BLOCK/PASS split is printed so a sweep that only ever produces one verdict cannot read clean. Both numbers are pinned. The scene-7 story in the retracted verdict was also wrong: scene 7 reaches npcMoveAngle ZERO times on every button out to 1800 frames, so it was never the blocking scenario -- that was an inference of mine layered on a memory note about Marle walking 439->7, where Marle is an NPC and not a party member. Every unported mechanism upstream shrinks the set of reachable scenarios, so a negative reached under a known-incomplete engine expires the moment anything upstream lands. EVERY gate reject returns CLC, which is mandatory -- CLC is what makes C0/CA76 POP the object; a reject returning SEC would jam it at the FIFO head forever. WHAT IS COMPARED, said plainly because this sweep runs code the port does not model: the ROM's class-0 handler continues past the commit into CC17-CDBE (a 16-tile blit through the $2180 WRAM port into $7F:3800+, a 7-table VRAM upload queue at $0940-$09A0, and a 4-entry OBJ template at $7F4802 + $1700,X). None of that is ported. So the compare is exactly the bytes the port CLAIMS: the carry, $0F01,X, $0BC0..$0BC3, $0D80,X and $1B00,X. Same discipline as VMDIFF_WMASK -- grade what we own and say so, rather than letting a green line imply more. THE ARENA HALF IS SWEPT SEPARATELY (7 routines x 81 pool states) because the CAD9 half only ever reaches CtArenaAlloc(n=1): the 2- and 3-slot claims and releases live behind classes 1 and 2, which are unported, so nothing else would exercise them. $0BC4..$0BC6 are seeded FREE on purpose -- otherwise a port that scanned one entry past the pool would usually hit an occupied byte and fail silently, and the check could not see the scan bound at all (measured: widening the bound left it at 567/567). 1152 class1/2-unported is the deliberate escape hatch, exactly like --sweepcb3a's mode2-noncommit: CtAnimDrainVisit returns -1 for classes 1 and 2, so scoring them as matches would be a lie and scoring them as mismatches would judge the function against a contract it does not have. Porting C0/CEF5 or C0/D4F7 MOVES that number and this check notices. ACCEPTANCE: 14 single-fact mutations were applied one at a time and ALL 14 turn it red -- the $1100 bit7 polarity (1536), the $1A81 BEQ and BMI rejects (384 each), the $0F00 window gate (384), the CC04 equality guard (48), the alloc-failure frame DROP (128), the arena's CONSECUTIVE requirement (arena 78), the 0x200 slot stride (128 + arena 52), the CDC1 INC (384), CDC1's index being the WORD $6D/$6E rather than the byte (192), class 3's CLC (576), EA42 freeing the whole RUN rather than one slot (arena 19), the unconditional follower writes in the n-slot free (arena 44), and the 4-(n-1) scan bound (arena 40). THE FIRST ACCEPTANCE RUN WAS ITSELF WRONG and it is worth recording why: it was a bash loop, and `\&` inside a double-quoted string kept its backslash while an anchor containing `||` was shredded by IFS='|'. Both made the compile fail, `>/dev/null` hid it, and the sweep silently re-ran the PREVIOUS binary -- reporting three real defects as invisible. The driver now asserts the anchor matches once AND that the build produced a newer exe. SCOPE CEILING. CtAnimDrainVisit is called from this sweep ONLY. Wiring it into --portrun's per-object loop was tried and MEASURED: 1592/1592 -> 156/1592. The reason is structural and worth keeping: C0/CAD9 is not a per-object per-frame function, it is driven by C0/CA76's FIFO, which visits an object only when C0/C98A enqueued it and pops it on the CLC. Called speculatively for every object every frame, every object claims an arena slot; the release lives in the draw pass C0/B701, which is unported, so from the fifth claim on E952 refuses and CC10's BCC drops the frame. The port was right and the harness around it was wrong -- closing that needs the FIFO ORDER and B701's release, not a different call site. --porttick 128/136 and --portrun 1592/1592 are unchanged. ==== RE-PINNED 19584 -> 80640, and 1152 class1/2-unported -> 2304 class2-unported: C0/CEF5, CLASS 1, IS PORTED. The sweep also gained $1B00,X as a swept INPUT (0x00/0x01/0x80/0x81), which is what class 1's pass select reads, so the case count is 4x. CEF5 IS NOT CLASS 0 WITH BIGGER NUMBERS -- its dispatch (CF0B-CF1E) is THREE-way. $1780,X == 3 takes CF21, a SINGLE visit that stages the whole two-slot run (32 tiles, CF6B `LDA #0020`), bumps $1B00,X by TWO (D11A + D11D) and returns CLC without ever reading $1B00,X. Otherwise ($1B00,X & $7F) == 0 takes D28A, PASS 1: resolve via C0/CB3A, the equality guard, claim TWO CONSECUTIVE slots via C0/E97A, commit $0F01,X, INC, and return **SEC** -- the first ported path that asks C0/CA76 to keep an object at the FIFO head. Anything else takes D30D, PASS 2, which does no lookup, no guard, no allocation and NO commit: it only stages the other 16 tiles at $0D80,X + $200, INCs and CLCs. So the entire frame decision lives in pass 1 and the mode-3 path. THE THREE `INC $1B00,X` DISAGREE ON INDEX WIDTH, which is a ROM fact and not a tidy one: D308 (pass 1) runs after `D304 SEP #30` so it is indexed by the BYTE $6D, while D4F0 (pass 2) and D11A/D11D (mode 3) run while X is still 16-bit (their `SEP #10` is at D4F3 / D120, i.e. AFTER) so those use the WORD $6D/$6E. Mutating that one asymmetry alone moves this check by 288. A DECODE TRAP WORTH RECORDING: a raw scan for `60` (RTS) in the pass bodies reports hits at CFC1 and D399 that do not exist -- both are the OPERAND byte of `STA $0960,X` (`9D 60 09`), the same false positive as CCA1 in class 0. Pass 2 has NO early exit; it was read from raw bytes, not from dis.py, which desyncs there. ACCEPTANCE for the class-1 half: 10 single-fact mutations, ALL 10 turn it red -- the mode-3 select (576), the `AND #7F` pass select (384), pass 2 not committing (768), E97A claiming TWO slots (960), the equality guard (192), the +2 in mode 3 (384), pass 1's SEC (576), D308's byte index (288), mode 3's CLC (384), and dispatching class 1 at all (1728). ==== RE-PINNED 80640 -> 165888 and 2304 unported -> ZERO: C0/D4F7, CLASS 2, IS PORTED, so every sprite class the dispatcher can reach is now graded. The sweep also gained $1B00,X values 0x02/0x82 (class 2 has THREE passes) and $0F01,X = 0x10. C0/D50D-D514 IS A TRAP AND IT IS CANONICAL: `LDA $1780,X / CMP #03 / BNE ->D515 / RTS`, and CMP with A == 3 leaves the carry SET -- so a class-2 object in anim mode 3 returns SEC HAVING DONE NOTHING, and C0/CA76 spins on it until the raster deadline. Verified from raw bytes (BD 80 17 C9 03 D0 01 60). That is also why CtAnimDrainPass's 64-visit guard is no longer merely a malformed-list backstop -- the ROM's own terminator here is the clock, which a clockless port does not have. SIX LEGS, TWO OF WHICH MATTER: $1B00,X & $7F picks the pass and $0D00,X == $68 picks one of two staging geometries, giving 2 x 3 bodies (phase 0 -> D546/D608 SEC, phase 1 -> D68B/D738 SEC, phase 2 -> D7E5/DA69 CLC). The two phase-0 bodies are BYTE-IDENTICAL through the entire frame half, so the $68 split never touches the frame decision -- it only changes the staging offset ($0100/$0200 for phase 1, $0400/$0300 for phase 2). `JSR CB3A` appears only at D546/D608 and `JSR E9AA` only at D555/D617, so the lookup, guard, allocation and commit ALL live in phase 0; phases 1 and 2 are pure staging with no early exit (their bodies contain no RTS at all). THE INDEX-WIDTH ASYMMETRY IS NOW A RULE, not an accident: every SEC (intermediate) tail runs after a `SEP #30` and is BYTE-indexed (D603/D686/D733/D7E0, and class 1's D308); every CLC (final) tail runs with X still 16-bit and is WORD-indexed (DA62/DD21, class 1's D4F0 and D11A/D11D, class 0's CDC1). ACCEPTANCE for the class-2 half: 13 single-fact mutations, ALL 13 turn it red. ONE OF THEM WAS A REAL HOLE IN THE CHECK FIRST: deleting class 2's equality guard changed nothing, because D514 sends mode 3 out with SEC BEFORE the guard, so the only $0F01 value that could match ($1301 = 0x14) never reached it. Adding 0x10 -- what C0/CB3A actually returns here, since a fresh-boot oracle leaves $1480/$1500/$1580 zero and the lookup lands on $E4:0001 -- made it visible (192). Class 1's guard had been graded all along via its mode-3 path CF21. The class-0 and class-1 acceptance drivers were re-run against the widened sweep and both still report zero holes, after four of their anchors had to be made unique -- classes 1 and 2 introduced textually identical lines, and an ambiguous anchor silently skips a mutation. ==== CLASS 0's TILE HALF (C0/CC17-CDBE) IS PORTED, minus the pixel copy, and the compare now includes it: the seven upload-queue tables $0940/$0950/$0960/$0970/$0980/$0990/$09A0 with their 16-bit terminator, the $79 cursor, and the 4-entry OBJ template at $7F4802 + $1700,X. WHAT IS IN IT: CC17-CC3B resolves the frame RECORD pointer on the SNES HARDWARE MULTIPLIER ($4202 = frame, $4203 = the class stride $28, product from $4216, plus $1380,X; bank $1300,X). CC78-CCB4 appends one upload job -- dstA = ($0D00,X & $1FF) << 4, srcA = the arena base, both duplicated at +$100, lengths $0100 -- then INCs $09A0 and STZs the NEXT slot, BOTH 16-BIT even though C0/CA76's prologue reads $09A0 8-bit. CCB6-CDBE writes five of each entry's eight bytes: +2/+3 the record's X displacement SIGN-EXTENDED, +4 its Y displacement, +6 ($0D00,Y & $FF) + e*2, +7 = $0F81,Y | $0D01,Y | ($0C01,Y when that entry's own +4 byte is >= $E8, else $0C00,Y). NOT PORTED: the 16-tile PIXEL COPY (CC3F-CC76 through the $2180 WRAM port, dispatching to C0/E687 verbatim or C0/E534 bit-reversed through the $C0:FD00 H-flip table). Its output lands in $7F:3800+, which is deliberately OUTSIDE the compare. Nothing else depends on it. 82944 class1/2-tilehalf: classes 1 and 2 append to the queue ONCE PER PASS with per-pass lengths (measured: C0/D394 `ADC #0200` inside class 1's pass 2), so a shared helper with different constants would be a guess. Those cases are counted, not compared and not hidden. ACCEPTANCE: 17 more single-fact mutations, all 17 red. FOUR OF THEM WERE HOLES IN THE SWEEP FIRST, and all four were SEEDING defects rather than port defects: with $09A0 starting at zero a 16-bit INC is indistinguishable from an 8-bit one and the 16-bit terminator STZ writes zeros over zeros (fixed by seeding $00FF and a poisoned next slot); and with a FIXED record base the sweep never reached a record with a negative X displacement or a Y displacement >= $E8, so the sign extension and the priority split were both unreachable (fixed by varying $1380 across the swept axes). The 16-bit INC took two attempts: the first fix was overwritten by an OLDER seeding block further down that re-zeroed $79 and $09A0 -- found by probing the live values rather than re-reasoning. All four earlier acceptance drivers were re-run against the widened sweep and still report zero holes (71 mutations across five drivers; the single known exception is --sweepdrain's SEC branch, stated in src/move.c). ==== THE PIXEL COPY IS PORTED TOO, so class 0's tile half is complete and the compare now includes the 2 KB staging pool $7F:3800-3FFF byte for byte. WHY IT PORTS AS ONE LOOP DESPITE TWO DIFFERENT WRITE PATHS: C0/E534 (tile-word bit14 SET) pushes 32 bytes through the $2180 WRAM port, which auto-increments, while C0/E687 (bit14 clear) sets DB = $7F and stores DIRECTLY to $0000,Y with Y = $D0, then RESYNCS the port with `TYA / CLC / ADC #0020 / STA $2181` (E72E-E735) so a following E534 continues from the right place. The caller keeps $D0 in step by adding $20 per tile (CC55), so both land tile t at $7F:($0D80,X + t*$20). E534 IS THE HORIZONTAL FLIP: every byte goes through $C0:FD00, an exact bit-reversal table, and since a 4bpp tile stores one pixel row per byte per bitplane with byte ORDER preserved, reversing each byte mirrors each row -- H-flip baked into VRAM, which is why the OBJ attribute carries no flip bits. E687'S BANK DISPATCH IS NOT A PASS-THROUGH, and this is the fact most likely to be got wrong: only $7F (E8C2), $D2 (E7BC), $D3 (E83F) and $D4 (E739) read their own bank; ANY other value of $CF falls through to C0/E6B6, which reads bank **$D5 HARDCODED**. E534 has no such dispatch -- its `[$CD],Y` honours $CF for every bank -- so the two copiers genuinely read DIFFERENT data when $CF is outside that set. They also differ in width: E534's `[$CD],Y` is a 24-bit add that can carry out of the bank, E687's `CLC / ADC $CD` is 16-bit and wraps. ACCEPTANCE: 14 more single-fact mutations, all 14 red. THREE WERE HOLES IN THE SWEEP FIRST, all from the same seeding defect: $CF was fixed at $D2, so the E6B6 fallback never fired, the two copiers never disagreed, and E691's 16-bit add never wrapped. Varying $CF over {$D2,$D6,$D3,$D4} and $CD over {0000,F000} made all three visible (864 / 792 / 1248) -- and the port stayed byte-exact through the change, which is the corroboration that the dispatch and both addressing modes are right rather than merely untested. NOT PORTED: $CF == $7F (E8C2 reads WRAM rather than ROM) is modelled but not swept -- a $7F base plus a high tile index would carry into bank $80, which romRead24 does not map. Across the whole C0/CAD9 family there are now 85 acceptance mutations in six drivers, with ONE known exception: --sweepdrain's SEC branch, stated in src/move.c. ==== CLASSES 1 AND 2's TILE HALVES ARE PORTED TOO, so NOTHING is excluded from the compare any more: 0 unported and 0 class1/2-tilehalf, over all nine staging legs and both class-2 geometries. TWO LAWS FOUND BY SCANNING EVERY LEG: the upload-queue append and the OBJ template happen ONCE PER SPRITE, in the pass that returns CLC (`STA $0950,X` exists only at CCA8, CFA8, D380, D858, DB17). Passes that return SEC stage tiles and nothing else. And the piece data always begins right after the tile-word array: LDY #$20 / #$40 / #$60 for 16 / 32 / 48 words. FIVE THINGS AN EXTRAPOLATION FROM CLASS 0 WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG, each verified from the ROM: (1) THE >= $E8 PRIORITY TEST IS CLASS-0 ONLY -- classes 1 and 2 contain ZERO `CMP #E8` and split by piece INDEX instead (0-3 take $0C00,Y, 4 and up take $0C01,Y). Counted: class 0 has 24 template stores for 4 pieces because the E8 test duplicates the +7 store, classes 1/2 exactly 5 per piece. (2) THE APPEND'S dstB AND srcB DO NOT SHARE AN OFFSET -- class 0 is +$100/+$100, class 1 +$100/+$200, class 2's non-$68 leg +$300/+$500 and its $68 leg +$100/+$100 -- and the two LENGTHS differ and are SWAPPED between the class-2 variants ($500/$100 vs $100/$500). (3) THE SECOND RUN OF EVERY TWO-SEGMENT LEG READS $0D80,X WITH THE **WORD** $6D/$6E, because those legs do a `REP #30` between runs (D5C4, D6F4, D7A1, DACE); every first run and every append uses the byte. Traced per site. (4) THE TILE NUMBER'S EXTRA $10 MOVES. There is exactly one `CLC / ADC #10` in each class-2 template: DA02 (non-$68) before the piece-8 store, DCA9 ($68) before the piece-4 store. Classes 0 and 1 have NONE. (5) THE RECORD POINTER MUST BE RE-RESOLVED AFTER THE COMMIT -- CC22/D2A3 feed the hardware multiplier from $0F01,X, which the commit just changed. Resolving it at entry (correct for the passes with no commit) cost 2112 mismatches until it was fixed. ACCEPTANCE: 21 more single-fact mutations, all 21 red, zero holes -- and the $68 geometry had to be put INTO the sweep first ($0D00's low byte == $68), or three of class 2's six legs were unreachable. The full family is now 106 mutations across seven drivers, with ONE known exception: --sweepdrain's SEC branch, stated in src/move.c. FOUR of the older drivers' anchors broke again when ctAnimStage was split into ctAnimRec/ctAnimAppend/ctAnimTemplate; they were re-anchored and re-verified.
checks.note_pass: CtAnimDrainVisit is byte-exact against a micro-executed C0/CAD9 over 165888 visits: all four sprite classes, all nine staging legs, the 2 KB pixel pool, the upload queue and the OBJ templates

mutations.find: if (r[0x1100 + idx] & 0x80) return 0;                   // CADE BPL: bit7 SET = destroyed/inactive
mutations.replace: if (r[0x1100 + idx] & 0x40) return 0;                   // CADE BPL: bit7 SET = destroyed/inactive
mutations.why: CADE tests BIT 7 of the actor state -- destroyed or inactive. All four of this routine's gates return CLC, which is what makes C0/CA76 POP the object; a gate on the wrong bit drains the wrong objects.

mutations.find: if (a == 0 || (a & 0x80)) return 0;                     // CAE5 BEQ / CAE7 BMI (any $01-$7F passes)
mutations.replace: if ((a & 0x80)) return 0;                     // CAE5 BEQ / CAE7 BMI (any $01-$7F passes)
mutations.why: CAE5's `BEQ` and CAE7's `BMI` are TWO tests on $1A81,X: zero means never placed, bit7 means hidden, and any $01-$7F passes. Dropping the zero test draws objects that have no position yet.

mutations.find: if (r[0x0F00 + idx] == 0) return 0;                     // CAEC: outside the camera window
mutations.replace: if (0) return 0;                     // CAEC: outside the camera window
mutations.why: CAEC: the camera-window latch C0/A88D wrote this frame. Without it the drain visits objects the activation gate has already rejected.

mutations.find: switch (r[0x1201 + idx] & 3) {                          // CAEE-CAFD: the sprite's PIECE COUNT
mutations.replace: switch (r[0x1201 + idx] & 2) {                          // CAEE-CAFD: the sprite's PIECE COUNT
mutations.why: CAEE-CAFD dispatches on the sprite's PIECE CLASS, the low TWO bits of $1201,X. A narrower mask sends class 1 down class 0's emitter and class 3 down class 2's.

mutations.find: default: return 0;                                    // CAFF CLC/RTS -- class 3 is never drawn
mutations.replace: default: return ctAnimClass0(r, rom, romLen, idx);                                    // CAFF CLC/RTS -- class 3 is never drawn
mutations.why: CAFF is a bare CLC/RTS: class 3 is NEVER drawn by this pass -- C0/E12A handles it. Routing it to an emitter here draws it twice.

checks.name: sweepdrain-b701-ca76
expect: sweepdrain: B701 release 192/192 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 0 emitters-left-unported); CA76 FIFO drain 2088/2088 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 504 clock-dependent, 0 unported-class, 0 lost)
checks.notes: The two ends of the sprite ARENA's lifecycle, which is a closed loop inside ONE frame: C0/00D3 A810 -> C0/C98A ENQUEUE (--sweepc98a), C0/00D6 CA76 DRAIN -> C0/CAD9 -> the E952 GRANT (--sweepcad9), C0/00DB B271 -> C0/B309 -> C0/B701 the FREE (here). B701's three JSRs to E9E2/E9FF/EA1F are the ONLY callers of the 1/2/3-slot frees in the whole ROM. B701 IS ONE LAW, NOT THREE ARMS. Verified against raw bytes: B716/B737/B75E are the same instruction sequence differing only in a threshold and two addresses. With T = (class & 3) + 1 = the arena arity and n = $1B00,X: if ((n & 0x7F) < T) { bit7 set -> reposition-emit and CLC; else SEC } else { instantiate-emit, free T slots, $1B00,X = 0x80, CLC }. The carry is the DRAW GATE -- its only caller C0/B309 does `JSR B701 / BCC -> draw / RTS`. Class 3 tail-calls C0/C73A, whose carry is NOT explicit (C73A has no SEC/RTS or CLC/RTS at all, only a bare RTS at C7FA, so it is whatever C7EF's `ADC #0008` left); the sweep MEASURES it rather than letting the port assert it. THE SIX EMITTERS ARE NOT PORTED, and that is safe rather than convenient: a scan of all seven (B788/B8CA/BA65/BCDC/BFF2/C2BF/C73A, 4216 bytes) finds ZERO reads and ZERO writes of $0BC0..$0BC3, $0D80, $1B00, $0F01 or $0F00 in any addressing mode -- absolute, indexed or long -- and no call into the arena or the frame lookup. They produce OAM records and nothing else. TWO SETUP DEFECTS THIS SWEEP EXPOSED IN ITS OWN EARLIER REVISIONS, both of which had made it green for the wrong reason. (1) DB WAS $7E. The field engine runs with DB = $00, where bank 0 mirrors the first 8 KB of WRAM AND maps the PPU registers; with DB = $7E the drain's `LDA $2137` read WRAM instead of latching the counter, so vCount stayed 0 and the raster deadline NEVER fired. Measured directly: `vPos=120 vCount=0`, then `A=0078 C=1` once fixed. The other three sweeps in this family were changed to DB = $00 too and are unmoved, because every address they compare is below $2000 where the two banks coincide. (2) THE QUEUE HELD CLASS-0 OBJECTS AND THE COMMENT CLAIMED THEY WERE 'REAL SPRITES OF THIS STATE'. There is no state -- this family's oracle is a fresh boot, so $1200/$1280/$1300/$1380 are all ZERO and C0/CBDC's tile blit dereferences a null 24-bit pointer ($CF = 00, $CD = 0000) and segfaults. The queue is now built from objects that reach CLC WITHOUT entering a handler -- class 3, plus one object failing each of the four gate tests -- which exercises the pop path identically, since CA76 cannot tell WHY CAD9 returned CLC. The visit itself is graded by --sweepcad9. THE CLOCK RUNS, and that is the real boundary. CtOracleRunToPC calls only cpu_runOpcode, but the CPU's read/idle callbacks drive snes_runCycles, so the V counter ADVANCES mid-drain exactly as on hardware. Measured: with the real budget $0078 and a start of 0x77 the oracle drains ONE object then stops, while the port (which has no clock) drains all three; and a start of 0xEF drains FULLY because the counter ticks into vblank during the prologue and CA97's signed BPL then lifts the limit entirely. So a case is GRADED only when its outcome is clock-independent -- already in vblank, already at/past the budget with 48 scanlines of headroom, or a budget above 261 that the counter can never reach. The other 504 are counted as clock-dependent and reported, never silently scored. The unreachable budget 0x0180 is also what makes the WORD-ness of CA99's `CMP $6B` observable: with only zero-high-byte budgets a port reading $6B as a byte goes unnoticed. ACCEPTANCE: 17 single-fact mutations, 16 turn it red -- B701's arity (52), its class-3 arm (32), the bit7 mask in the threshold (21), bit7-means-released (24), freeing T slots rather than one (28), the $80 stamp (96); CA76's $09A0 prologue gate (1044), `STZ $79` (1044), the vblank lift (216), >= vs > (72), the word budget (108), the bit7 empty test (moves 684 cases to unported-class), the $6D latch (540), head==tail emptying BOTH ends (540), the head advance (540), nulling the popped link (540). THE ONE THAT DOES NOT: the SEC branch (`keep the head, do not pop`) is UNGRADED. The only C0/CAD9 paths that return SEC are the class-1/2 multi-pass handlers, which CtAnimDrainVisit refuses with -1, so every object the sweep can legally queue returns CLC and deleting the branch changes nothing observable. It is derived, not verified. Porting C0/CEF5 or C0/D4F7 makes it gradable. SCOPE. Neither routine is wired into any live path; both are graded here only. --porttick 128/136 and --portrun 1592/1592 are unchanged. ==== CLASS 0's TWO OAM EMITTERS ARE PORTED (C0/B788 reposition, C0/B8CA instantiate) and the compare now includes the live OAM records at $7F:4BC0 + $1700,X and the high-table byte at $7F:4F00,X. 192 -> 144 graded because class 3 moved into the counted bucket (see below); 144 cls1-3-emitters are the cases whose emitter is not ported. THE RECORD IS NOW FULLY ACCOUNTED FOR: the template writes +2/+3 (X displacement, sign-extended), +4 (Y), +6 (tile) and +7 (attribute); the emitters compute +0 (on-screen X low byte) and +1 (on-screen Y). +5 is written by neither. B8CA is B788 plus the staged->live copy, which is exactly why B701 may free the arena slot at that instant. THE X HALF WALKS BACKWARDS, and that is load-bearing: each piece folds bit 8 of its X into an accumulator as `A = ($E5 << 2) | bit8`, so going from the last piece down puts piece 0 in bits 0-1 -- the SNES OAM high-table layout. Only the X bit is accumulated; every SIZE bit comes from one `ORA #$AA` at B7D0. On the final iteration `CPX $D9 / BEQ` fires BEFORE the store, so the finished byte only ever reaches $4F00,X. ==== A CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS COMMIT'S DOSSIER, which claimed $C6 at B7D9 was the camera window's bottom edge left over from C0/A8BF. IT IS NOT. `B796 STA $C5` runs with M SIXTEEN-BIT, so it stores (screen Y & $01FF) across $C5 AND $C6 -- the emitter clobbers the camera value two instructions in. The two tests at B7D9 and B836 are therefore one Y-RANGE CLASSIFIER on the object's own screen Y: >= $100 -> path A, $80..$FF -> path B, <= $7F -> path C. The sweep proved it: seeding $C6 independently produced 48 mismatches until the port read bit 8 of the screen Y instead. AND THE THREE PATHS DO NOT WRITE THE SAME NUMBER OF RECORDS: counting `+1` stores per path, identically in both emitters, path A writes FIVE ($4BC1/$4BC9/$4BD1/$4BD9/$4BE1) and paths B and C write four. The X half is a loop over four. So the `Y >= $100` case writes one record more than the template ever filled. CLASS 3 IS NOW REPORTED AS UNDERIVED rather than assumed. C0/B785 tail-calls C0/C73A, which has no SEC/RTS or CLC/RTS anywhere -- only a bare RTS at C7FA -- so its carry is whatever its last ADC left. This check used to pin `return 0` for it, MEASURED; that measurement only held while $1700 happened to be zero, and seeding $1700 for the emitters exposed it returning SEC. CtAnimRelease returns -1 there now. A constant that was right by accident is exactly the kind of thing this family's discipline is meant to catch. ACCEPTANCE: 14 more single-fact mutations, all 14 red. ONE WAS A HOLE FIRST -- path C's `BPL` versus a carry test was unreachable because the screen Y and the $1B00 value were both driven by the same sweep index, and $80 (the only n selecting the reposition emitter) fixed the Y. Decoupling them made it visible (5). The family is now 120 mutations across eight drivers, with ONE known exception: this check's SEC branch. ==== ALL SIX CLASS-0/1/2 EMITTERS ARE PORTED. cls1-3-emitters 144 -> 48: only class 3's C0/C73A is still counted. checks.name: sweepaba2-heading-builder
expect: sweepaba2: C0/ABA2 (heading builder) vs micro-execution -> 10000/10000 byte-exact over the WHOLE 128KB image (0 mismatch, 0 lost)

checks.note_pass: C0/ABA2, the field HEADING builder, byte-exact against micro-execution over the WHOLE 128KB image: 10000/10000 across the cross product of the four staged bytes, PLUS an EXHAUSTIVE second phase at 261121/261121. THIS WAS THE LAST KNOWN DEFECT IN THE MOVER CHAIN -- with it fixed, --sweepops goes 1050/1080 -> 1080/1080, all 18 opcodes 60/60, zero differing addresses. THE DEFECT: the ROM compares the RAW staged bytes with `SEC / SBC / BCC`, an UNSIGNED borrow, and takes NO arguments; the port took SIGNED int8 deltas its caller had computed. At the map wrap the two disagree -- target $00 from current $FF BORROWS in the ROM but truncates to +1 as an int8 -- so they aimed 180 degrees apart, which negated the velocity exactly. It also writes five bytes the old version never touched: $01EF, $01F6, $01F7, the 16-bit pair $01F4/$01F5, and $01EE. Two of the four quadrant arms SWAP $01F6/$01F7 through the accumulator's hidden B half (XBA), and one path writes $01F7 TWICE. SEED GRID: the four bytes swept over {00,01,1F,20,3F,40,7F,80,FE,FF} -- $00/$01 and $FE/$FF straddle the unsigned wrap (the defect itself), $1F/$20 and $3F/$40 straddle the two BIT #$40 / BIT #$20 scale selectors. All four quadrants and all three scale arms are reached, the counts are IN THE PIN, and the mode FAILS if any arm count is zero. NARROWER STACK EXCLUSION THAN --sweepops, ON PURPOSE: that sweep skips [$01F4,$0200) because its opcodes nest calls, but ABA2 contains no JSR and CtOracleRunToPC sets PC directly, so only the fake return address at $01FE/$01FF is touched. Excluding just those two lets this grade $01F4/$01F5 -- and that matters: `AC0D/AC30/AC50 STA $F4` is a SIXTEEN-BIT store, and mutating it to 8-bit drops the score to 2916/10000. ALL SIX DERIVED FACTS MUTATION-TESTED: signed instead of unsigned dy -> 7400/10000 (i.e. this check catches the very defect it was built for), un-swapping quadrant 1 -> 7638, 8-bit STA $F4 -> 2916, mask $7F instead of $7C -> 7684, dropping the STZ $EF -> 0. A no-op control stays at 10000, so the test is not trivially red. PHASE 2 ANSWERS THE COVERAGE QUESTION INSTEAD OF ASSUMING IT. Phase 1 sweeps 10 values per byte, i.e. 10^4 of a 256^4 input space, which on its own proves nothing about reach. It does not have to: every output depends ONLY on the two (delta, borrow) pairs, because the only things read from $01F0-$01F3 are the two `SEC / SBC` results and their carries. Per axis that is 511 reachable combinations -- 256 without a borrow (cur $00, tgt d) and 255 with one (cur $FF, tgt d-1) -- so 511x511 is EXHAUSTIVE BY CONSTRUCTION, not by sampling, and it runs in ~4.5s. Phase 1 having compared the WHOLE 128KB image is what licenses phase 2's narrow 7-byte compare: phase 1 establishes WHICH bytes are written, phase 2 checks their VALUES everywhere. Mutation-checked on both: the signed-delta defect reads 7400/10000 in phase 1 and 130816/261121 in phase 2.

That is a LIFETIME divergence, not a missing feature, and it is what made the sound mailbox $1E00-$1E03 vanish the moment the player stepped onto the overworld, where there is no scene to hold it. IT PINS THE CLAIM, NOT AN IMAGE. --wramlife stamps 0xA5 into six probe addresses after each location load and reports, on the next one, which survived. The expected pattern IS the derivation: $1D40 and $1940 DEAD because they sit inside C0/7F95's $7E:1D00-1DFF and C0/58B9's $7E:1900-19FF; $1CFF and $1A00 ALIVE because they are the bytes immediately outside those two windows, so an off-by-one clear shows up here and nowhere else; $2A00 ALIVE because a location change touches ZERO bytes of $7E:2A00-2FFF (wram_lifetime.md sec1, measured over four transitions); $8000 ALIVE as a far-from-anything witness. THE COUNT IS IN THE PIN because 6/6 is the whole verdict. MUTATION: restoring the old `memset(m->s, 0, 0x10000)` at the top of memLocationLoad reads `2/6 as derived, 0 alive` -- every probe dead, including the two the ROM leaves alone. No pre-existing check caught that mutation; field-worldtest-roundtrip, field-worldtest-audio and field-newgame-pan all passed WITH the wipe in place, which is exactly why this one had to be added rather than assumed covered. NOT PROBED: the mailbox page itself, even though it motivated the change -- the song staging writes $1E00-$1E03 on every load (C0/1B5F) and the Akao driver owns the rest, so a sentinel there reads dead for reasons unrelated to lifetime. field-worldtest-audio covers the mailbox; this covers the rule. This one drives ACROSS the hop, 370 frames of it on the overworld.
`project: hop CROSSED` is frame-free on purpose and is the proof the run actually got there -- without it a drive that stalls in the forest reads exactly like a clean crossing. The f-numbered `hop at fN` line is for humans and is NOT pinned, so an unrelated re-time cannot fail a check whose subject is only 'did it cross'. Same rule for the RECONVERGED windows: the VERDICT WORD is pinned, the frame spans are not.
THREE VERDICTS, AND THE THIRD IS THE POINT. At a transition the two machines load at their own pace, so 'they differed at some point' is the wrong question. RECONVERGED = disagreed for a window and then agreed to the end; that is a SETTLE-TIME offset, not a broken port. Measured here:
  pos      apart f29..f153, together for the LAST 245 frames. Our overworld entry finishes ~70 frames before the ROM's, so the two players read differently while the ROM is still loading -- and then match exactly, both walking south and both STOPPING ON THE SAME BLOCKED CELL (280,312). The world mover and its collision agree with the ROM. The compared address is $0283/$0285, NOT the mover block's own $0D84/$0D88. The lead's block is first-fit allocated (C2/048A, base $0C30, 60 slots) and lands at a DIFFERENT address per world ($0D70/$0DF0/.../$0CF0 for worlds 0..7), so $0D84 is a world-0 coincidence -- src/main.c's --checkowmove hard-codes it and therefore misreports the player on worlds 1-7. $0283/$0285 is the world-independent anchor the ROM's own entry scanner (C2/3287) and music-zone object (C2/2FEE) read; it is written every traveling frame by C2/3739/C2/373F and SEEDED AT LOAD by C2/2270B. Measured: it reads the right (280,280) from the moment we enter, while $0D84 still holds load garbage (14336,272) until the block is placed at T0+62 -- and from f124 the two agree exactly. Using $0D84 made the harness report that garbage as a divergence for 16 frames.
  song     apart f29..f69.   tilemap  apart f15..f62 (the ROM starts loading the world map at the fade, we finish sooner; both then hold the same 96x64 block grid).
loc WAS the second live finding and is now FIXED (see below); it reads RECONVERGED apart f28..f28 -- a
single-frame offset at the commit, which is the comparison seam (the oracle runs its whole frame before
we run ours, so a quantity committed on frame N reads a frame early on its side).
  THE FIX: our exit path filled C variables and never performed the ROM's STAGING, so the commit --
  which was already ported, byte-for-byte, in CtSceneTick -- had nothing to fire on. field.c now runs

NO LIVE FINDINGS LEFT. Every projection is CLEAN or RECONVERGED; a DIVERGED here is now a regression, not a known gap.

So the check now runs with CT_AUDIO_FORCE=1 + SDL_AUDIODRIVER=dummy, exactly as field-worldtest-audio does, and mail RECONVERGES -- apart f0..f87, together for the last 311. The opening window is our driver booting from a mid-game seed (it stages the current song 08 while the oracle's driver settled that long ago); it is a settle difference and RECONVERGED is the honest word for it.

RE-PIN RULE: DIVERGED -> RECONVERGED or CLEAN is an improvement (verify against the oracle, re-pin, say so). RECONVERGED -> DIVERGED is a regression. A new name in the list is a regression.

THE ALGORITHM GRADED AGAINST THE CARTRIDGE. saves/ct_real_save.srm is the 8 KB SRAM image lifted out of saves/com_jogo_salvo.state — a game the ROM itself saved — and 0x6B8C is the word the ROM wrote at $30:7FF0. checks.notes:
THE SAVE, and its jingle. ROM C2/CF37 is one routine whose FIRST four instructions are the sound -- `LDA #19 / STA $1E00 ; LDA #8A / STA $1E01 ; LDA #80 / STA $1E02 ; JSL $C7:0004` -- and whose rest is the write: `LDX $79 / LDA #FF / STA $0D49,X` then `JSL $FF:F9FB`. The jingle stages the mailbox DIRECTLY, never through the stager C2/EB03, so it never touches $0D76 and can never be throttled -- unlike every blip on this screen.
FF/F9FB packs EIGHT records named by the table at $FF:FA7B ({srcAddr:2, srcBank:1, len:2}) CONSECUTIVELY into the slot (Y is loaded once at FF/FA2A and the MVNs leave it advanced): $7E:2400+0x5B0, $7E:2C23+0x33, $7E:0400+0x10, $00:0100+0x10, $7F:0000+0x200, $00:027E+2, $00:0290+0x11, $7E:2C7C+0x1E = 0x0834 bytes. Slot bases are the ROM table $FF:FBE1 = $30:6000/$6A00/$7400; CT's HiROM SRAM window is $30:6000-7FFF so the image offsets are 0x0000/0x0A00/0x1400. Then FF/FBE7's checksum at $30:7FF0+slot*2 and the $E41B signature at $30:7FF8+slot*2. Dossier: disasm/notes/save_write.md.
⭐ VALIDATED AGAINST A REAL ROM SAVE. saves/com_jogo_salvo.state is a game the ROM itself saved: repacking that state's OWN WRAM with this record table reproduces its SRAM slot 0 in 2098 of 2100 bytes -- the two that differ are $7E:0400/0401, the play clock, which ticked between the ROM's save and the state capture -- and running FF/FBE7 over it yields 0x6B8C, the exact word the ROM stored.

CT_SRAM_FRESH=1 boots from an ERASED cart (0xFF) and ignores any .srm on disk -- without it the second run of this check would find the slot it wrote on the first and take the occupied branch, so the check would pass once and lie ever after.
WHAT IS PINNED IS WHAT IS ROM-DERIVED: the pack LENGTH 0x0834 (the sum of the record table's eight lengths) and the $E41B SIGNATURE, both read back OUT of the image after the write. The checksum VALUE is deliberately NOT pinned here -- it moves with the live game (the play clock alone changes it), and a signature that moves for reasons the check does not model is a signature that will be re-pinned without thought. The checksum ALGORITHM is graded where it is invariant instead, by field-save-checksum-vs-real-rom-save. For the record: the signature is what FF/F9C4 tests and the checksum is FF/FBE7 run over the whole $0A00 slot -- tail included, which is why the erased cart's 0xFF matters. What used to sit in field.c was an invention: a square-ish `dx <= 10 && dy <= 12` box, NEAREST-wins, plus a hand-added "reach one tile further when the faced tile is solid" rule. The ROM's box is DIRECTIONAL and asymmetric -- 28 px along the faced axis, 12 px to either side (#01C0 / #00C0 in 12.4) -- it scans objects HIGH index to LOW and takes the FIRST hit, and it needs no counter rule because 28 px already reaches ~1.75 tiles.

The check used to stand the player at (392,112) -- 32 px from the curtain, OUTSIDE the ROM's 28 px box -- and only the invented extra reach made it work. Our player CANNOT get closer: from (392,112), holding Up for 10, 24, 40 or 60 frames leaves them at exactly 112.0, so a tile the ROM lets the foot enter reads solid here. The oracle walks to 103.94. That is a COLLISION defect (~8 px, the lower half of tile row 6), NOT a probe defect, and it is now visible instead of compensated for. This check deliberately does not grade it -- it stands the player where the ROM stands and grades the PROBE.

checks.notes: USER REPORT (translated from Portuguese): 'when two enemies are killed with one cyclone, both do the dissolve animation, but only one of them makes the sound'. The death sound is not a per-kill event fired at damage time -- it is part of the DEATH ROUTINE, and the routines are serialized. CD/0043 (vector #12, entered from CF/FE76 with A = the dying combatant) is one corpse's whole death: the $CCEA wait, then `LDA #95 / JSR CD/3B71` with X = $1D0C[$CD00] as the pan. battleAdvanceDissolves already runs those routines ONE AT A TIME, highest combatant index first (battle_death_dissolve_order.md: both oracle runs go cmb4 then cmb3, +43 frames apart, whichever way the hit-set order is flipped), but the SOUND was armed for every kill on the damage frame and fired for all of them on the same frame -- two #95 posts into one driver tick, of which only one is audible. ORACLE, the same forest double kill (forest_cyclone = forest_holdleft_pre.state + $2837|=0x80, `--monitor 7E1E00:4 --writer --diff`): `f708 id 95 pan 58` then `f751 id 95 pan 78` -- TWO posts 43 frames apart, pan 58 = cmb4 and pan 78 = cmb3 (the dissolve order), each one frame after its own routine starts (delist f707 -> cmb4 done f750 -> cmb3 done f793). The fix holds a queued corpse's countdown until its dissolve is the one running. WHAT THIS PINS: the ORDER (cmb4's pan 58 first) and the SEPARATION (ours 41 frames against the oracle's 43 -- our dissolve run is CT_DISSOLVE_HOLD+STEPS long, which is a separately pinned quantity, so the 2-frame gap is the run length's, not this gate's). checks.notes: THE MOVER FROM A MID-BATTLE SEED, GRADED AGAINST THE ORACLE FRAME FOR FRAME AND PIXEL FOR PIXEL. wa2158.raw.wram is the oracle's WRAM one frame before f2158 of forest_wait_ambush_active.state (`--peek ... --btnscript "0:2158"`): enemy slot 5 (the Avian, id $19) has $5E0D=0A requested over a live $974A=0F with a segment IN FLIGHT ($98A7=1, $9737=4, $9819=1); slots 1/2 are Beetles (id $8D) in mode 01. CT_BATTLE_MVSWEEP seeds every per-slot mover byte from the image (CtBattleMoverSeed) and steps the idle walk + the mode machine + the mover 72 frames; sf=k is oracle frame 2157+k. ORACLE (`--monitor "7E1D14:1,7E1D2B:1,7E974A:8,7E98A7:8,7E9737:8,7E9786:8,7E9897:8" --input "0:2260" --diff`): f2158 the group-2 visit commits 0F->0A (C1:336A) WHILE the segment runs -- phase 5 lands the same frame (Y A2), 6 at f2162 (A1), 7 at f2166 (A0), the end at f2170 (9F, CF:F9A2/F9A5); the handler counter $9897[5] wraps at f2178 (C1:372F) and class 6 starts its first segment there (C1:3F52, angle 00, C1:3EC3) with $9819 left at 04 -- NO decrement on the start frame -- so phase 1 lands f2182 (X 8A), 2 at f2186 (8B), ... 8 at f2210 (91); the next segment starts f2218, phase 1 f2222, 2 f2226 (92). And the Beetle of slot 1, at (120,150) with its stored bearing $9791=1 and Crono at (110,176): its passes at f2173 and f2213 INC $9829 (C1:3836) and write $98A7 := 0 (C1:384F) -- ARRIVED, no segment, because |dx|^2+|dy|^2 = 776 <= 0x400, the mode-1 threshold of C1/2AEF -- no box overlap anywhere near. WHAT THIS ENGINE PRINTS: the same events on the same sf. It pins four mechanisms at once: (1) the commit writes nothing to the mover -- the in-flight segment continues through its phases 6/7/8; (2) the mover runs BEFORE the handler pass within a frame (CF/F978 from the per-frame service path, C1/3714 in the idle tick), so a segment's first step is `period` frames after its start, not period-1; (3) the per-slot cadence $9742/$98C2 (E4/F609 >> 4 / & 7), reloaded on the wrap and never re-seeded at a segment start; (4) the class-1 arrival is the DISTANCE test by mode (C1/3813: 0x400 / 0x1000 / 0x10 for modes 1/2/3, else arrived) -- not the box overlap the port used to test, and not the 'ready-hold' it used to have. The class-6 orbit itself (the halved radius of mode 0A, the ellipse's +0x20 X, the angle) is what produces the 8A..91 X track. CT_BATTLE_SCHEDPHASE=3 / CT_BATTLE_MVCADPHASE=2 are the seed's five-frame phases, MEASURED from the oracle's $A4 INC and $9897 DEC frames (f2160/2161/2163 and the skip at f2160/2165/2170) -- constants of the capture, not of the engine. ==== 2026-09-18, THE MAIN LOOP'S TWO-FRAME ITERATION (the zelda3 model; disasm/notes/oracle_logical_frames.md §4). The battle's idle loop waits twice per iteration (C1/109D, C1/10BD): frame A runs the walk dispatch and C1/10BB STZ $E5, frame B C1/10C4 INC $E5 and the tail (timers, cursors, handlers), then the next head's C1/8121 INC $0027. The three rates this file carried -- the logic tick at 2.5 frames, the $A4 INC at 3 of 5, the mode pass at 4 of 5 -- were fits of the REAL cartridge's lagging iterations; the logical oracle runs every iteration in two frames, and the port now does: $A4 is the NMI's CF/E3F8 INC on $A013 = 0 and $E5 != 0, an enemy turn is C1/4058's two waits (CT_BATTLE_ENEMY_THINK 3 -> 2, the demo's C1/4058 3 -> 2), the first head is the entrance loop's end + CT_BATTLE_BOOT_CPU 0. battle-gato-fight-vs-logical-oracle grades the whole GATO fight against the logical oracle frame for frame; the ATB fills ~20% faster than on the lagging cartridge (song end -> attack A 231 against 279). This check moved with it and was re-pinned. NOW GRADED AGAINST THE LOGICAL ORACLE (tools/sweep_logical_cmp.py): the seed is re-made from its state (PEEK_SAVE, its WRAM checked identical to the committed image), the logical oracle continues it, and every mover step (mode, foot) the sweep prints is compared on the oracle's frame; the port's own trace lines are echoed after the verdict and stay pinned. The seed's $E5 gives the iteration's phase, so the envs CT_BATTLE_SCHEDPHASE / CT_BATTLE_MVCADPHASE are gone.

checks.notes: THE VICTIM'S RECOIL IS THE VICTIM TRACK'S OWN `A9 dd`, run by the interpreter's move-forward mover -- not a knock applied at a strike constant. GATO's physical (CD/7A42, mask 9000: roles 0 and 3) puts `76 00 03 | 0C | A9 04` on role 3 = the primary victim ($A014[3]). ROM: C1/6AF0 arms the mover of the combatant of the role RUNNING the track ($A639 := dd, $A34A := the `76` bearing $A5AA -- unquantized, atan2 by C1/0222 -- base $A35D/$A370 := the foot, $A311 := 0, $A19D := 0, $A337 := 1) and falls into its own VISIT (C1/6B46): finished -> stop; the point 16 px ahead on the bearing hits the grid ($7BFD & C0) -> stop; C1/7C2B (the foot's box vs every body) -> stop; DEC $A639 / BNE stay. Every frame while parked: the SERVICE first (CF/F194, on the rate divider: the foot at the arena's edge tiles -> finished; DEC $A639 / BEQ finished with no step; $A311 += $A324 (the `0C` speed, CC/F4BC); foot = base + trig(bearing, acc)), then the visit again. ORACLE (gato_press_action --input "100:8,0:1900", `--monitor "7EA639:1,7EA337:1,7EA324:1,7EA311:1,7EA19D:1,7E1D23:1"`): f535 $A324 := 04 (C1:4F79, the `0C`); f536 the arm ($A337 := 1, C1:6B46) and the arm's visit ($A639 4 -> 3, C1:6B91); f537 the service (CF:F1B6 $A639 := 2, CF:F1C2 $A311 := 4, CF:F1E7 $1D23 90 -> 93) then the visit stops on the grid (C1:6B97 $A337 := 0); nothing at f538. Marle at f1800/1801: the same shape with bearing 0D -> (B0,6F) -> (B3,70). So `A9 04` is exactly ONE step of the speed on the frame after the op, along the aimed bearing, and only if the way 16 px ahead is clear -- a second hit on a victim already against the wall moves nothing. WHAT THIS ENGINE PRINTS: `asc ... t3 FWD n=4 speed=4 rate=1 head=40 from=(134,144)` at the op, `ascfwd ... cmb0 cnt=2 acc=4 head=40 pos=(134,147)` the frame after, `stop(grid)` in the same frame; the second attack on the parked Crono stops at the arm (no step); Marle's hit prints her own step with an unquantized head. (The port's dispatch marker sits 4 frames before the ROM's -- rel 54 here for the oracle's rel 58 -- the standing pre-roll residue; the mechanism is graded relative to the op.) ==== 2026-09-18, RE-PINNED (the battle opening, disasm/notes/battle_boot_turns.md): its content moved with the fight: a fixed frame now falls where GATO / the Hetakes stand at another point of their wander, or where the actions came in another order, and the HUD's gauges read other values. The enemy AI runs one entry per turn on the ROM's own pointer ($B1D4/$B1E4, C1/8C3E + C1/8CF9): GATO's op 00 move is a TURN WITH NO ACTION (the cartridge's f892), so his song comes one ATB later (cartridge $A013 f1151 = fixture f925); the eval writes $AEE3 = the op it pre-reads (C1/8CE0 -- the cartridge's 01 00 01 at f376, 00 00 06 at f635); and the turn no longer draws a target (the cartridge's turn draws only the damage pipeline), so HP values and targets that ride the RNG index moved to the cartridge's draw count. THE ROM'S LAW, in two routines: (1) C1/B3BB, called from C1/813A (defeat), C1/8176 (victory), C1/821B and C1/83A3 (flee) -- the only four call sites in the image -- runs `$29C6 + 12*slot &= 0x40` over all EIGHT staged slots; (2) the field epilogue C0/07ED reads that byte back, `LDA $7E29C6,X / BNE ->080D`: nonzero = restore the object's field position, zero = dead-mark it ($1000,Y |= 0x80, $1A81,Y = 0). Bit 6 is set at STAGING by C0/05B2-05C2 (`LDA $1100,Y / CMP #06 / BNE / ... ORA #40`) = the field object's MOVE-MODE is 6. So a staged enemy's object survives IFF it was staged with move-mode 6 -- independent of whether it died, dissolved or fled. CT's line-break codes come in pairs -- 0x05/0x07/0x09 are a bare newline, 0x06/0x08/0x0A are 'newline THEN INDENT THREE', and 0x0B/0x0C are the page break's two (assets/text.py _NAMES). The indent lives INSIDE the token; the ROM's typewriter C0/2126 handles a control code in one iteration and then calls the renderer once, so the indent is never typed. The fix carries the distinction in the asset instead of guessing it back: pack_dialogue passes ind='\x02'*3 and TB_IND draws like a space but costs no iteration. checks.notes: C2/8ECC's AMOUNT, graded against the CARTRIDGE. Every expected line here was measured on the oracle with `--callrom C2/8ECC` (disasm/notes/menu2_tech_effect.md AV.1, an adversarial second pass that re-wrote the model from the ROM bytes and swept 26 cases); this check just prints what our port computes for the same inputs. The two arms: an ITEM sets $0DBF to a constant with bit7 SET and gets a FLAT ($0DBF & 0x7F) * ($0DC0 & 0x0F) -- Tonic = 0x32*1 = 50 -- while a TECH sets $0DBF to the caster's DERIVED MAGIC (sheet +0x39) with bit7 clear and gets $0DBF * ($0DC0 & 0x1F) plus a per-target spread ((($0DBF+1) & 0xFF) * rnd) >> 8, the six rolls read from C0/FE00 in REVERSE at cursor $7E:0D00. checks.notes: THE MENU WINDOW GRADIENT IS GENERATED, AND THIS GRADES THE GENERATOR AGAINST THE OSCILLOSCOPE. The dark menu windows are shaded by HDMA channel 0 writing $2131/$2132 (CGADSUB + COLDATA) once per scanline: a grey fixed colour ADDED on the way down each window and SUBTRACTED on the way out -- one 16-step ramp +8..-7 in 5-BIT colour space that RESETS and HEIGHT-NORMALISES per window. C2/86DD builds that table from a WINDOW LIST of [kind, height] pairs (kind 0 = flat band, 1 = ramp, 0x80 = end) at ROM $FF:BBF2, one per ribbon option, copied to $7E:9D99 by the bank-FF block copier C2/F362 (writer C2:F376, measured). The per-step line count is hi($A01B += height*16) with $A01C zeroed after each step, so the step size is height/16 with the remainder CARRIED -- which is why 192 -> 12 scanlines, 160 -> 10, 144 -> 9, 128 -> 8, 80 -> 5, 48 -> 3 and 32 -> 2 all fall out of ONE routine. EVERY EXPECTED BAND HERE WAS MEASURED ON THE ORACLE'S OWN HARDWARE with `ct.exe --hdma saves/com_jogo_salvo.state --btnscript "0:20,200:2,0:40[,80:2,0:8]*N"`, whose `scanline trace` section reports the fixed colour and sub flag the PPU actually saw each line (one line later than the table entry -- the HDMA latency). Compared row by row against this generator: 224/224 scanlines identical on ALL SIX options. WHAT IT REPLACED: three baked tables, each one instance of this machine -- ctMenuWinGrad (the status screen's single 192 ramp), ctMenuItemGrad and ctMenuSaveGrad5. Every screen that was not special-cased was painted with the STATUS list, so the Tech, Config and Form windows ran one continuous 192-line ramp down the whole screen instead of restarting per box: on the Form screen the third party panel and the Exchange window faded to black, which is what made a party exchange unreadable. Switching the whole chrome to the generated ramp plus the exact 5-bit COLDATA model took the opt-0 frame from 24.3% to 59.3% pixel-identical against the oracle capture scratchpad/menu/or_opt0.png (pixels off by more than 4: 10257 -> 5187), and the generator reproduces the pixel-exactly-derived ctMenuSaveGrad5 at all 224 rows with ZERO mismatches -- which is the independent proof that the transcription is right. NOT GRADED, ON PURPOSE: the fractional carry ($A01C is zeroed, not the whole accumulator). Every ramp height in the six X-menu lists is a multiple of 16 (192/160/144/128/80/48/32), so the remainder is always zero and a mutation that drops the carry SURVIVES. That is a fact about the lists, not about the routine -- the lists after $FF:BC38 (the shop screens, which this port does not reach) begin `flat 8` and would exercise it. Do not add a mutation for it without a reachable witness. THE CALL SITE IS GRADED ELSEWHERE: this mode calls the generator directly, so a mutation that feeds the WRONG list to the chrome painter cannot be seen here. It lives on menu-ribbon-select-colors, which hashes a rendered opt-4 (Form) frame.
