checks.name: field-party-gate-operand-source
expect: gateop: op=CF arg=02 ip 0344->034B carry=1
checks.note_pass: the $C2 family reads its operand from the SCRIPT, and 0xCF branches on ABSENT
checks.notes: THIS CHECK EXISTS BECAUSE OF A DEFECT THAT SHIPPED AND THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD SEE. When the $C2 family body was lifted out of move.c's switch into the shared CtVmPartyGateFamily, it kept move.c's own operand reads -- `r[0x12001 + ip]`, i.e. the ROM's $7F:2001 -- which are correct for CtFieldRunnerOne (that caller passes script = r + 0x12001, so the two are the same pointer) and WRONG for ct_vm.c, where the script is host memory and `addr` is body-relative. --sweepops is structurally blind to it: it grades only the caller for whom the pointers coincide, which is the blindness class in ct-sweepops-blindness-classes. field-party-gate-live-vm could not see it either -- 0xF8/0xF9/0xFA read NO operand, and they are the only arms a headless drive can reach without a textbox. Scene 41 obj10 slot3 is `CF 02 05` at body 0344: op 0xCF (has-character), operand 02 = Lucca, branch displacement 05. Lucca is absent, and 0xCF takes its jump when the leaf returns NONZERO (the OPPOSITE polarity to the $C1 side's 0xC9), so the target is spill + disp = 0346 + 05 = 034B. THE IP IS THE DISCRIMINATOR, not the printed arg: with the operands read from $7F:2001 the same run reports `ip 0344->0347`, the fall-through -- a different control flow, on the check's own line. CT_CALLFN is what makes the site reachable: it lives in fn slot 3, which no other headless driver enters.

checks.notes: THE DECISION BOX'S CURSOR MACHINE, $0162-$0166 (disasm/notes/textbox.md). Found because the user's own F5 snapshot read $0162 = 0 where the ROM reads 1 at the same station. $0162 is a four-state machine that owns the input frame while a decision box is up: 1 = requested (the op's C0/3695-3697, alongside $0165 = operand2&3 and $0164 = (operand2>>2)&3), 2 = cursor LIVE (C0/202D-202F), 3 = CONFIRMED (C0/1AF9-1AFB, the A handler). The box machine's state 7 branches on it BEFORE it ever reads the press latch (C0/201C): 0 -> the plain $0134 path, 1 + $0215 == 0 -> arm the cursor, 2 -> RTL and nothing, 3 -> close. So on a decision box the A press is NEVER $0134. $0215 is why a MULTI-PAGE decision costs two presses: at the end of a non-final page the pending break code is still there, so C0/2027 sends it down the ordinary page turn and only the LAST page arms the cursor. Before the port the port ran every decision down the PLAIN-TEXT path with a host re-implementation (nopt / choiceSel / CtSceneChoose) and spent the press on a latch the ROM does not read. $0215's SEED: C0/1FCD writes it when it creates the window, not only at the reveal's end -- oracle f212 (box 0x2B requested, byte still the previous box's 00) -> f217 (window created, byte = 04) -> 0x10 while typing, the break code as each is consumed, and at state 7 the code the string ENDED on (0C on 0x2B's page 1, 00 on 0x29's option page, which is the one that lets the cursor arm). DERIVATION, all measured: (1) the opcode jump table, read out of the ROM at $C0:5D6E + 0x94*2, holds 5215; (2) C0/5215 resolves its operand as an object OFFSET (5223 `LDA $7F2001,X / TAX`) and then falls STRAIGHT INTO 5228 -- the same body op 0x95 reaches by `5426 BRL ->5228` after resolving through the party-slot table, and the same body 0xB5/0xB6 reach through C0/3546/354F; (3) 5228's arrival test is 5245-5252 (Y) and 5254-5263 (X), each a WRAP-EXACT 8-bit `CMP / INC A / CMP / DEC A DEC A / CMP` on the tile bytes $1801/$1881 -- ADJACENT, not equal -- after which 5265 tests `$1C81,X` bit 1 (C0/30B3) and 5273 does `JSR C0/568B` + TYX/INX/INX/SEC, i.e. COMPLETE with IP += 2. Before the fix the same run finished at f288 on tile (5,9), obj2's OWN tile: a tile too far and 24 frames late. ⚠ HONESTY ABOUT WHAT IS PINNED: the frame NUMBERS are our own trajectory (no oracle state exists for any of the 30 locations that use op 0x94, so this cannot be a lockstep), and a future mover fix may move them -- re-pin then. mutations.why: MVN $7E,$7E moves between WRAM banks, and WRAM is 8 master cycles an access, not the 6 a FastROM byte costs (snes_getAccessTime). LakeSnes re-fetches the three opcode bytes per byte moved (cpu.c case 0x54 does pc -= 3), so a byte is 18 + 8 + 8 + 12 = 46; charging the two data accesses at 6 makes every match 4 cycles a byte cheap and the model stops matching the ROM on all nine packets.

mutations.find: if (idx & 0x80) continue;                          /* the loader's own BMI: bit 7 = no packet */
mutations.replace: if (idx == 0xFF) continue;   /* MUT: only $FF means no packet */
mutations.why: Every site tests its index byte with BMI (`C2/278A`, `27F4`, `2837`, ...), so ANY value with bit 7 set means 'this world has no such packet' -- not just $FF. World 2's header switches three sites off that way, and reading only $FF as absent sends the loader to pointer-table entries that are not packets at all.

C2/2757-275B indexes the world header table with `ASL A / TAX / LDA $C6FD00,X` -- a WORD per world, not a 3-byte pointer like the packet tables. A stride of three reads another world's header and the whole packet list changes. (Graded on world 2 and not world 0: 0*2 and 0*3 are the same index, so the world-0 check cannot see this one at all.)

THE GATE IS AN OBJ PRIORITY-0 SPRITE AND THE WINDOW IS WHAT MAKES IT VISIBLE. User report (translated from Portuguese): "the circular portal shown at the moment of the F5 is not visible or did not render properly" -- in the port the Telepod gate was a thin black/white RING at the rim of an otherwise untouched room; in the game it is a filled blue vortex.

THE RULE, FROM THE PPU ITSELF. Mode 1's layer order is a list of (layer, priority) SLOTS, not of layers: snes/ppu.c layersPerMode[1]/prioritysPerMode[1] -- the table the oracle actually renders with -- reads OBJ3, BG1.1, BG2.1, OBJ2, BG1.0, BG2.0, OBJ1, BG3.1, OBJ0, BG3.0, backdrop. So an OBJ priority-0 pixel loses to BG1/BG2 at EITHER priority and to BG3 priority 1, and to nothing else -- which is why a `8E 00` object is normally invisible in a room and why this port turns one into a see-through-to-the-map STENCIL. But ppu_getPixel folds the WINDOW into the same test as the enable bit (`mainScreenEnabled && (!mainScreenWindowed || !ppu_getWindowState(...))`), so a layer a window masks off this pixel is not in the list at all. checks.name: sweepaitarget-b8bb-resolvers
expect: sweepaitarget: C1/B8BB resolvers vs micro-executed bank-$C1 handlers -> 1065/1065 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 0 lost); counts seen: 297 empty / 534 single / 234 MULTI; 84 of them a4e0-tailed (count+winner excused, every other byte compared), 15 rom-nonterminating (measured: the oracle did not return)

sweepaitarget: C1/AC14 targeting request vs micro-executed C1/AC14 -> 1335/1335 byte-exact (0 mismatch, 0 lost) over $AECC[0..10], $AD8E[0..10], $B2AE and the $B1D2 cursor; 270 took the LITERAL arm ($AD8E left all $FF by AC2A's BRA), 387 resolved to NO TARGET ($B2AE = $FF, not the lead PC), 84 a4e0-tailed, 15 rom-nonterminating
checks.notes: THE FIRST BANK-$C1 MICRO-EXECUTION HARNESS IN THIS TREE, and it exists because battle_enemy_move_target.md SS G.5 said to build it before porting anything. Every other runSweep* in main.c drives bank $C0/$C2; the battle engine had no equivalent at all, so a resolver ported against nothing would have been a check that grades agreement instead of correctness ([[check-vs-own-reference]]). WHY A SWEEP AND NOT A SCENARIO: the targeting byte is witnessed taking 00/01/04/05/06/0A/0E/0F/10 across nine captures, but those are MID-BATTLE states, which do not seed the port. Seeding the input space directly is the only honest way in -- the same argument --sweepdraw's refusal arm made. WHAT THE ROM ACTUALLY DOES, and why the port's old shape could not express it: C1/B8BB's handlers do not return a target, they FILL A LIST at $AECC with the count in $AECB. Value 01 (C1/A3F7) is ALL LIVING PCs, 02 (C1/A411) all living combatants out to seat $0A with X CARRIED OVER from 01's loop, 03 SELF ($B252+3), 04 a STORED target out of $B19E[$B252*4] & $0F. Values 0A-0D and 0E-10 are ONE machine: C1/AE70 tests seat $AF1E's block byte at `+$0A` against the mask $AF1F -- skipping $AEFF,Y == $FF and block +$1D bit7 -- appends the seat and ORs in two flag bits off block +$20 with their counters $AF20/$AF21; then C1/ADA1 reduces the list against the last-target ring $B23A[0..7]. ENTRY STATE, none of it guessed: DB = $7E (C1/AE70's `LDA $0000,X` indexes a block base ABOVE $2000, which bank 0 does not mirror), DP = 0, M 8-bit, X/Y SIXTEEN bits (`CPY #0003`, `LDX #0002`). Decoding this block with 8-bit X desynchronises it into BRK/WAI garbage, which is what had made the family look unreadable for months. The PC comes out of the ROM's OWN table at C1/B8BB[value*2], never a list written in the harness, so a mis-transcribed entry address cannot hide. THE COUNT TALLY IS PART OF THE CHECK. `270 empty / 404 single / 180 MULTI`: a family whose every case resolved to exactly one target would be indistinguishable from the single-seat model this port used to carry, so `MULTI` reaching zero means the sweep has stopped exercising the one thing that makes the ROM's shape different from ours. THE TWO SKIP CLASSES ARE MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED -- the port decides them, so leaving them on trust would let it delete its own mismatches from the denominator. (1) `a4e0-tailed`, 56 cases: C1/ADA1 tail-calls C1/A4E0 when $AF20 != 0 and the winner has bit $40, and A4E0 descends into C1/0003 -> C1/2986, which branches on $96F5,X / $9FF7,X -- two bytes NOTHING in this engine writes (SS F.4), so porting it would repeat the $A2B5 mistake. Those cases still micro-execute and still compare every byte A4E0 cannot touch; only $AECB and $AECC[0] are excused. (2) `rom-nonterminating`, 10 cases: C1/ADA1 variant A's `BPL ->ADB3` (ADD1, offset $E0 = -32, bytes `B9 CC AE 10 E0`) branches back to the COMPARE with both cursors unchanged, so a ring match on an entry whose bit7 is clear re-tests the same entry for ever. That is the ROM's own non-termination, not the port's, and the harness PROVES it: it runs the oracle on those seeds anyway and FAILS if the ROM returns. SCOPE: values 05 and 06 are deliberately outside the grid -- 05 draws the battle RNG and 06 descends into C1/2986's ungated bytes, and both already have their own wrapper and their own grading. 07-09 and 11-17 are underived. NOTHING is wired: CtBattleAiResolveList is graded here only, and battleAiTarget still resolves 05/06 and falls back to the lead PC for the rest. Changing that needs the LIST to reach the action layer, which is its own pass. ACCEPTANCE: 10 single-fact mutations, all 10 red. ONE WAS A SURVIVOR FIRST, and it was COVERAGE, not code: reading C1/A3FD's `CMP #FF` as a bit7 test passed, because every seeded $AEFF value was $00-$20 or $FF and the two readings never disagreed. A fifth SEAT row of $80/$FE/$81/$F0/$8F -- bit7 set but NOT $FF -- separates them, and took the grid 854 -> 1065 cases and MULTI 180 -> 234 on the way. Same shape as --sweepdrain's path-C hole: an input the seeds could not produce, not a rule the port had wrong.
checks.note_pass: C1/B8BB's twelve ported targeting resolvers are byte-exact against micro-executed bank-$C1 handlers, list and flag counters included

mutations.find: for (int y = 0; y < 3; y++) {                               // A3F9-A40A: the three PC seats
mutations.replace: for (int y = 0; y < 2; y++) {  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/A3F7's loop is `CPY #0003` -- the THREE party seats. Two drops the last PC out of every list value 01 and 02 build.

mutations.find: if (s[0xAEFF + y] == 0xFF) continue;                      // A3FA LDA $AEFF,Y / CMP #FF
mutations.replace: if (s[0xAEFF + y] & 0x80) continue;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/A3FD is `CMP #FF`, an EXACT compare, not a bit7 test. $AEFF holds char ids, and an id with bit7 set is not the absent marker -- the ROM only skips $FF.

mutations.find: if (s[base + 0x1D] & 0x80) { s[0x0D] = 0; return s[base + 0x1D]; }   // AE97 LDA $001D,X / AE9A BMI -- dead
mutations.replace: if (0) { s[0x0D] = 0; return s[base + 0x1D]; }   /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/AE97's `LDA $001D,X / BMI` is the dead gate -- block +$1D bit7, the same byte battleAlive reads. Without it dead PCs enter the candidate list.

mutations.replace: if (s[base + 0x20] & 0x10) {  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/AEAF tests bit $20 for the $40 flag and C1/AEC1 tests bit $10 for the $80 flag. Swapping which bit arms which flag moves both $AF20/$AF21 and the entry bytes -- and $AF21 is what selects C1/ADA1's variant.

mutations.find: int base = rom[ROM_CMB_BLOCK_TBL + x] | (rom[ROM_CMB_BLOCK_TBL + x + 1] << 8);   // AE80, long,X
mutations.replace: int base = 0x5E2D + x * 0x20;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/AE80 reads the block base out of the ROM table $FD:A80B (5E2D 5EAD 5F2D ...), a 0x80 stride on a seat*2 index. Halving it puts seats 1 and 2 at 0x5E6D/0x5EAD, so the filter reads the wrong stat byte and the wrong dead flag.

mutations.replace: int variantA = 0;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/ADAB's `LDA $AF21 / BEQ ->ADD8` picks between two scans that differ only in ADCE's extra `LDA $AECC,Y / BPL`. Forcing variant B makes the first ring match win even when its bit7 is clear.

mutations.replace: /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/AE18 masks the surviving entry back down to its seat nibble, stripping the $40/$80 flags C1/AE70 ORed in. Without it the list's single entry carries flag bits the ROM has removed.

mutations.find: case 0x00: return 0;                                          // C1/A3F6: a bare RTS -- sets NOTHING,
mutations.replace: case 0x00: s[0xAECB] = 0; return 0;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/A3F6 is one byte, `60` -- a bare RTS. It writes NOTHING, not even a zero count, and the sweep poisons $AECB precisely so that 'writes nothing' is a graded fact rather than an assumption.

mutations.find: int x = (s[0xB252] * 4) & 0xFF;                             //   computed one. ASL/ASL are 8-BIT;
mutations.replace: int x = (s[0xB252] * 2) & 0xFF;  /* MUT */
mutations.why: C1/A441 is `ASL A / ASL A` -- the $B19E record stride is FOUR bytes, not two.

mutations.find: s->cpu->dp = 0x0000; s->cpu->db = 0x7E; s->cpu->a = 0; s->cpu->x = 0; s->cpu->y = 0;   // DB: C1/AE70 blocks
mutations.replace: s->cpu->dp = 0x0000; s->cpu->db = 0x00; s->cpu->a = 0; s->cpu->x = 0; s->cpu->y = 0;   // DB: C1/AE70 blocks
mutations.why: DB = $7E is not decoration: C1/AE70's `LDA $0000,X` indexes a block base above $2000, which bank 0 does NOT mirror, and $AECC/$AEFF are $7E addresses too. With DB = $00 the oracle reads open bus and the harness must go red rather than quietly grading a different routine. (The anchor carries the site comment because the SAME entry-state line now appears three times in main.c -- phase 1, phase 2 and --sweepmoveclass -- and the runner refuses a find that matches more than once rather than grading the wrong one.)

mutations.find: for (int x = 0; x < 0x0B; x++) { s[0xAECC + x] = 0xFF; s[0xAD8E + x] = 0xFF; }   // AC48-AC54
mutations.replace: for (int x = 0; x < 0x0B; x++) { s[0xAECC + x] = 0x00; s[0xAD8E + x] = 0x00; }   // AC48-AC54
mutations.why: C1/AC46 fills both lists with $FF, not 0. This is the byte that makes "no target" expressible at all: a resolver that appends nothing leaves $AECC[0] = $FF and $B2AE = $FF. Zero would be seat 0 -- the first PC -- so this mutation silently retargets every unresolved request onto Crono.

mutations.find: for (int x = 0; x < 0x0B; x++) { s[0xAECC + x] = 0xFF; s[0xAD8E + x] = 0xFF; }   // AC48-AC54
mutations.replace: for (int x = 0; x < 0x11; x++) { s[0xAECC + x] = 0xFF; s[0xAD8E + x] = 0xFF; }   // AC48-AC54
mutations.why: the clear's length. `CPX #000B / BCC` is ELEVEN entries, not the seventeen the sweep compares -- so $AECC[$0B..$10] must keep whatever was already there. Only poisoning the full compare window and clearing the ROM's shorter one catches this.

mutations.find: int value = rom[ROM_AI_SCRIPT_BANK + x];                        // AC1E LDA $CC0000,X
mutations.replace: int value = rom[ROM_AI_SCRIPT_BANK + x - 1];                    // AC1E LDA $CC0000,X
mutations.why: the cursor is advanced BEFORE the value is read (AC1A `INX` precedes AC1E). Reading at the old cursor takes the PREVIOUS script byte as the targeting value while still storing the advanced cursor, so $B1D2 agrees and everything downstream of it does not.

mutations.find: s[0xAECC] = s[0xAED8];                                        // AC24/AC27 -- and NO $AD8E copy
mutations.replace: s[0xAECC] = s[0xAEE5];                                        // AC24/AC27 -- and NO $AD8E copy
mutations.why: the literal target's source. $AED8 has exactly one writer in the whole ROM (C1/AF0E `LDA $AECC / AND #0F / STA $AED8`) and one reader, AC24 here. $AEE5 is the decoded targeting byte the OTHER entry path uses -- the plausible confusion, and a different byte.

mutations.find: s[0xAECC] = s[0xAED8];                                        // AC24/AC27 -- and NO $AD8E copy
mutations.replace: s[0xAECC] = s[0xAED8]; s[0xAD8E] = s[0xAED8];                 // AC24/AC27 -- and NO $AD8E copy
mutations.why: THE ASYMMETRY. C1/AC2A's `BRA ->AC3F` jumps PAST the copy loop, so on a bit7 value $AD8E stays all $FF from the clear while $AECC[0] carries the literal. Mirroring it too is the natural tidy-up and it is wrong; only comparing both lists in full can see the difference.

mutations.find: for (int k = 0; k < 0x0B; k++) s[0xAD8E + k] = s[0xAECC + k]; // AC33-AC3D, UNCONDITIONAL
mutations.replace: for (int k = 0; k < 0x0A; k++) s[0xAD8E + k] = s[0xAECC + k]; // AC33-AC3D, UNCONDITIONAL
mutations.why: the mirror's length, again `CPX #000B`. One entry short leaves $AD8E[$0A] at the clear's $FF while $AECC[$0A] carries a real seat -- invisible unless the list actually reaches eleven entries, which value 02 (all living combatants) is what makes it do.

mutations.find: s[0xB2AE] = s[0xAECC];                                          // AC3F -- on BOTH paths
mutations.replace: s[0xB2AE] = s[0xAECD];                                          // AC3F -- on BOTH paths
mutations.why: the single-target shadow is the list's FIRST entry. This is the exact fact that retires battle_enemy_move_target.md ?G.4's claim that reducing a multi-target list to one target would be an invention -- `AC3F LDA $AECC / STA $B2AE` is the ROM doing it, so getting the index wrong has to be red.

expect: sweepmuldiv: battleMul16/battleDiv32 vs micro-executed C1/C90B + C1/C92A -> 1452/1452 byte-exact over the WHOLE 128 KB image (only the RTS sentinel excused; 0 mismatch, 0 lost); 726 multiply cases, 726 divide, 126 of the divides take an early exit ($28 or $2A zero), 252 multiplies leave a non-zero HIGH word in $2E; the divide's PHP byte at $01FD is the ONE address excused, on 726 of its cases
checks.notes: C1/C90B and C1/C92A, the battle engine's SOFTWARE MULTIPLY AND DIVIDE, micro-executed against battleMul16 / battleDiv32. IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE PORT DID THE ARITHMETIC INSTEAD OF THE ROUTINE. Every battle formula that multiplies or divides goes through these two and reads the answer from $2C; the port computed the quotient in C, which gives the same number and none of the state -- and the state is load-bearing, because C1/DC64 CHAINS them: the multiply leaves its high word in $2E and the divide picks it up as the middle word of a 48-bit register ($2E is the one word C92D/C92F deliberately do NOT clear). The compare is the whole 128 KB with $28/$2A/$2C/$2E/$32 poisoned first, so a word left alone has to be SEEN left alone. THE ONE EXCUSED ADDRESS IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: the first run had all 726 multiplies exact and all 726 divides red, every one at $01FD with the port at 00 and the ROM at $26/$27 -- the P register with and without carry -- while the direct-page words matched on both sides. C1/C92A brackets itself in PHP/PLP so the caller's flags survive, and this port has no processor-status register to push; the byte is excused for C92A only, and the multiply going anywhere near it turns its cases red. Both carry-in values are swept because the multiply's first `ROR $2A` shifts the CALLER's carry in -- it never reaches a tested bit, so the product is unaffected and only $2A's final value carries it. Eight mutations, eight red.

mutations.replace: for (int i = 0; i < 15; i++) {                              // C90D LDX #0010
mutations.why: C90D's `LDX #0010` -- SIXTEEN steps, one per bit of the multiplier. One short leaves the product halved and the last multiplier bit untested.

mutations.replace: if (!c) {                                                  // C916 BCC ->C91F
mutations.why: C916's `BCC ->C91F` SKIPS the add when the carry is clear, so the add happens on a SET bit. Inverting it accumulates the complement of the multiplier.

mutations.replace: (void)a2A;
mutations.why: THE MULTIPLY DESTROYS $2A and the ROM leaves that destruction visible: the multiplier is rotated out a bit at a time and the accumulator's carries rotate in behind it. Writing the input back, or not writing at all, is the tidy-looking mistake -- and it is only catchable because the sweep compares the whole image instead of just $2C.
C91F/C921 rotate the 32-bit accumulator RIGHT THROUGH THE CARRY -- the bit the ADC pushed out is what re-enters at the top. A plain shift drops it and the high half of every product is wrong.
C939's `LDX #0020` -- THIRTY-TWO steps, because the dividend is 32 bits wide ($28 with $2E above it). Sixteen produces the quotient of only the low half.
C931 and C935 are TWO early exits, on a zero DIVIDEND as well as a zero divisor -- and both return with $2C already zeroed rather than trapping. 126 of this sweep's divide cases take one of them.

mutations.find: if (!c) { a32 = (a32 + a2A) & 0xFFFF; c = 0; }            // C94B restore / C951 CLC
mutations.replace: if (!c) { c = 0; }            // C94B restore / C951 CLC
mutations.why: C94B-C951 RESTORES the remainder when the subtraction borrowed -- that is what makes this a restoring division. Without it the remainder walks off and the quotient with it.

mutations.find: int a2E = s[0x2E] | (s[0x2F] << 8);                         // carried IN, not cleared
mutations.replace: int a2E = 0;                         // carried IN, not cleared
mutations.why: C92D/C92F clear $2C and $32 and DELIBERATELY NOT $2E: it is the middle word of a 48-bit register and arrives holding whatever the caller left -- in C1/DC64, the multiply's high half. Zeroing it is the assumption that makes `hit * 100 / evade` in C look equivalent to the chain.

C914's `ROR $2A` rotates THROUGH THE CARRY, so the caller's carry enters at bit 15 and, after sixteen steps, lands at bit 0 -- which is why the multiplier word ends holding the accumulator's carries rather than its input. Dropping the rotate-in is only visible where $2A is compared straight after the multiply: inside C1/DC64 the next instruction overwrites it, and a mutation declared there survives.

Five single facts of this routine were declared against field-battle-miss-forced and four survived; two of those turned out to be graded by field-battle-atk-header (the rand divisor and the clamp constant, both of which its pinned hitroll lines carry), and the rest were genuinely unreachable -- above all C1/DC99's `>=`, which differs from `>` on exactly one value in a hundred and which no fixture's draw ever lands on. This sweep sweeps the $26 cursor until sixteen cases DO land on it, and the report asserts that count so the boundary cannot go quiet again. Building it also forced two prerequisites into the port: C1/C90B and C1/C92A as routines (--sweepmuldiv) and C1/AF22's own state, since the ROM's modulo IS that divide and it leaves $32 behind. TWO EXCLUSIONS, BOTH MEASURED AND BOTH REPORTED: the nested call chain's STACK (C1/DC64 -> C90B, C92A, then AF22 which pushes $2C and calls C92A again, which pushes P) down to the deepest address the oracle actually touched -- $01F7, printed rather than assumed -- and nothing else. ⚠ WHAT THIS DOES NOT GRADE: the staging in the CALLER. It was port-side invention, measured dead across all ten battle scenarios, and deleted.) Eight mutations, eight red. !! ONE MUTATION WAS WITHDRAWN, and the reason is a fact about the routine: passing 0 instead of DC66's carry into C1/C90B survives, because DC84's `LDA $18 / TAX / STX $2A` OVERWRITES the multiply's leftover $2A with evade on the very next instruction. The carry-in is unobservable from inside DC64 by construction; it is graded where it is visible, in sweepmuldiv-c90b-c92a.

The bank-$C1 micro-execution harness built for --sweepaitarget is what makes them gradable, and this is that harness pointed at C1/3760. THEY ARE NOT PARAMETERS OF CLASS 1, which is why a fall-through was never going to be close enough: class 1 keeps a STORED bearing while $9791,X is set and these four always re-base and re-aim; class 1 arms $98A7,X at the END on the clear path and these arm it BEFORE the tests and only disarm on the stop; class 1 stops on a DISTANCE threshold and DEFLECTS when blocked, while class 2 has no distance test anywhere -- a blocked step IS its arrival. Class 3 is the axis-locked charge: the bearing is one of four cardinals chosen by comparing the target's coordinate with the enemy's own, on Y when the dispatched mode is 08 and on X when it is 09, and it also stops when the two coordinates land in the same 32-pixel cell -- which is all C1/0119 (`LSR A` x5) measures. Class 7 is a COMPASS charge with no target at all: the bearing comes from the mode, and four of its eight modes force an explicit facing index instead of the $C0F700 lookup. Class 7's `else` arm is NOT dead code -- it is mode 0x18. THE HARNESS TAKES BOTH ENDS FROM THE ROM: the seeded $A2B5 goes through CC/FBAB to a class, and the handler's ENTRY ADDRESS comes from C1/3760[cls*2] rather than a list written in the sweep, so neither a mis-transcribed address nor a mis-read class table can hide. WHAT IS COMPARED: every persistent byte the four write -- $9786 (bearing), $96DE (facing), $98AF/$98B7 (segment base), $98A7 (armed), $9829 (arrival counter), $5E1D (the split commit), $9831/$9839 (the victim's recorded foot), $A039/$A050 (the C1/283D mirror the step lands in), $A5FD and $9875 -- all POISONED first, so a write the port misses is as loud as a wrong one. That is what grades classes 7 and 8 NOT clearing $A5FD and class 8 not touching $9875 at all. EXCLUDED: $80/$8C/$8E/$AE/$DB/$D3-$D6, the ROM's direct-page scratch, which are C locals in the port. THE ARMED/STOPPED TALLY IS PART OF THE CHECK (340 / 470): class 2's whole point is that a blocked step is its arrival, so a grid that never blocked would leave every stop path unexercised and the sweep green for the wrong reason. TWO SETUP DEFECTS THIS SWEEP EXPOSED IN ITS OWN FIRST RUNS, both of which had made it wrong rather than merely incomplete. (1) X AND Y ARE SIXTEEN BITS. The handlers' bare `LDA $DB / TAX / LDA $C0F700,X` looks like it demands a narrow X -- it does not, because C1/01F9 returns with the accumulator's B half already cleared (`29 FF 00`, a 16-bit AND #00FF, at C1/0205). The width is settled by two three-byte immediates an 8-bit decode turns into garbage: `C0 0B 00` at C1/2914 is `CPY #000B`, not `CPY #0B` + `BRK`, and `E0 00 02` at C1/0208 is `CPX #0200`. Run narrow, the CPU went off into bank 0 at $FF1C on every case reaching C1/28B0 -- 756 of 810 lost, which is how the mistake surfaced. (2) C1/28B0 READS PRE-BUILT BOX ROWS. Only the ACTOR's $975A/$9770/$9765/$977B are rebuilt by the handler's own `JSR C1/285A`; every other body's come from C1/283D, which nothing in a sweep runs. Without seeding them the oracle compared its boot zeros against a port that recomputes from the mirror, and all 132 overlapping-body cases disagreed. They are now seeded from C1/285A's OWN formula -- whose clamps branch on the SIGN OF THE POSITION, not on the arithmetic result -- which is what lets this sweep grade battleBoxAt rather than assume it. ONE INPUT IS FORCED INTO AGREEMENT RATHER THAN GRADED, and it is named: C1/28B0's presence gate reads $96F5,Y while this engine reads $2980 / the staged record's +6 bit7, a stand-in recorded in battle_enemy_move_target.md §F.4 because nothing in the port writes $96F5. The sweep seeds all three consistently so the body test is exercised and comparable; the handler is what is under test, not the substitution. WIRED, not sweep-only: all four are dispatched by battleMoveTick now. No fixture arms them, so it is inert for the suite -- but the ROM's own table dispatches them, and a port that HAS a handler and refuses to call it is less correct than one that does.

THE HDMA WALKER against the CARTRIDGE, and BOTH SIDES ARE DERIVED LIVE -- there is not one pinned register value in this check. The port's render used to draw a whole frame from a single vblank latch; sequence-table entries 0 and 3 rewrite PPU registers every scanline (sequence_table.md 7.1/7.2), so the render is now driven by a per-line register file, and this grades the thing that fills it. Transliterated from snes/dma.c: dma_initHdma at line 0, dma_doHdma at the end of every visible line, bAdrOffsets/transferLength verbatim, indirect mode with the last-active-channel special case.

HOW IT RUNS: the oracle is booted to a frame inside entry 0 (the motorcycle race, six channels), `ct.exe --hdma` prints the colour-math state of every scanline of that frame, and the same run's .wram sidecar supplies the 64 KB $7E page the channels' tables are scattered across. `Belthasar --seqhdma` replays the walker over that page and the two are expanded to a per-line map and diffed. The pinned line is a COUNT (224 of 224) and the number of band changes, so a walker that flattened the trace could not pass by matching fewer lines. The run also refuses if the boot frame is not in entry 0 ($0384) or the six channels are not enabled ($038C), which is what stops a moved boot timing from grading an empty frame.

NO CAPTURE IS COMMITTED: saves/ is gitignored on purpose (the repo regenerates ROM-derived captures), so the page image is rebuilt into build/ each run.

TWO THINGS THIS CANNOT GRADE, as prose rather than green mutations: reading an indirect channel's DATA through $4307's bank instead of $4304's is invisible because $7E:36CC stores the SAME bank to both, and ignoring $2132's channel-select bits is invisible because entry 0's $EE sets blue, green and red at once. Both are modelled the way the hardware works.

A THIRD MUTATION WAS WRITTEN, SURVIVED AND WAS DELETED rather than kept as decoration: dma.c's rule that a terminating INDIRECT channel which is also the last active one fetches only the high byte of the next pointer. Entry 0 cannot grade it -- none of its six channels terminates inside the 224 lines. It stays in the code because that is what the hardware does, and entry 3 WILL reach it: its ch2 and ch3 run `hold x70` then `hold x1` and terminate at line 71. Re-add the mutation when that stage exists.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT GRADE: a pixel, and the WINDOW registers -- entry 0's trace does not report window state. Those wait for entry 3's render.

checks.note_pass: the effect programs' window rasterizer (op D9: clamp, angle, corners, scan conversion through $2180) is the ROM's own on 6000 micro-executed cases
checks.notes: USER REQUEST 'keep porting the x-strike's effects'. X-Strike's slash is two PPU windows: program op D9 n k (CD/19B1) clamps the segment $5DA0+4k to x 08..F8 / y 08..D4 (CD/2433), takes its angle through CE/E7CF (C0:F300), builds the four corners at half-width $5D8E across it (CD/2466, CD/3BFD on CE:F48E) and D1/F9AF scan-converts the quad into the window buffer not on screen (CD:38AA by $7C & 1 and n & 1): a 4-pass bubble sort on y (swap on >=), three edge layouts (flat top FA29, FA68, FAE8), 8.8 slopes through the hardware divider (x/0 = FFFF), 16-bit accumulators whose carry chains line to line after one CLC per section, the high byte of each `STA $217F` landing in WRAM through the $2180 port and two `LDA $217F` reads stepping over the other window. The sweep micro-executes CD/19B1 in the oracle (M8 X16 DB 7E, operands behind $40) on 6000 seeded cases over the whole byte range, both parities, and compares $5DA0..$5DAB, $CD08, $CC64, $CD0D..$CD1D and $C100..$D1FF (poisoned first) with battle.c battleFxLine. It is a sweep because the attract reaches D9 with inputs one frame apart from the port's (the interpreter's known +1).

checks.name: sweepshake-cd06b4-cd0b51
expect: sweepshake: CD/06B4 + CD/0B51 vs battleScrollFill + battleFxPalCommit -> 6000/6000 byte-exact (0 mismatched, 0 lost); liveness: 3537 re-rolls X, 2300 steps down, 821 steps up, 1775 axes turned off, 3572 re-rolls Y, 2250 waved fills, 1200 bit-7 / 1200 bit-0 commits
checks.note_pass: the battle NMI's scroll-record fill (CD/06B4, four variants) and screen shake (CD/0B51 -> CD/0C48) are byte-exact to the ROM on 6000 seeded states
checks.notes: THE BATTLE NMI'S CD/0929-092C PAIR (disasm/notes/battle_effect_orbit.md section 8), micro-executed on the oracle against battle.c. CD/06B4 `LDA $CA92 / ASL / TAX / JMP ($06BC,X)`: variant 0 (CD/06C4) fills the 32 per-line scroll records of BG1 ($BC89/$BC8B = $2C70/$2C72 + the shake $CCA4/$CCA6 + $BB01/$BB03), BG2 ($BD09 = $2C74 + $CCA8 ..) and BG3 ($BD89 = $2C78 + $CCAC ..) the HDMA channels 1-3 read; variant 1 (076C) takes BG3 from the effect program slot 0's anchor + offset ($CA5A + $CA5E); 2 (07E2) adds a per-record line wave $0A00,X where $CC91/$CC93/$CC95 say so; 3 (07B9) also BG3's records 32..63. CD/0B51 is the SCREEN SHAKE (the port had called it a palette 'wave' and refused to run while it was on): per axis (X $CCB0.., Y $CCB8..) a re-roll counter ($CCB2 vs $CCB3) redraws the random byte from C0:FE00[A + $7C + 1] (CD/0B16 `ADC $7C`; the carry is the CMP's; A = the counter for X, #40 for Y), an amplitude counter ($CCB4 vs $CCB5) walks the amplitude $CCB6 one step toward $CCB7 (a DEC to 0 turns the axis off), and the offset is the product's high byte (random x amplitude, $4217); $CCC0's six bits hand the two offsets to the layers' pairs (16-bit, high byte 0); an axis that is off zeroes its three pairs.
